The Spirit II E-310 Gas Grill turns out to be the little BBQ grill that can get the job done. I am pleased with it's construction, performance and grilling results.

title: Fancy, Stylish, Portable, Compact
text:
This is a nice grill design for items that you will watch closely.  It is an attractive unit.  Its single burner design doesn't allow for a cooler place on the grill to get indirect heating.  Setting the heat only sets the rate of heating, not the temperature.  This makes it imperative that you periodically raise the lid to regulate the temperature for items that are thicker.  Flare ups are common as the lid is vented on both sides and the grease hole in the bottom is large.  This is an open single burner and heats up very quickly.   So, it takes some time to get used to this grill.  Once you understand how this grill cooks you can adapt your cooking method to achieve very good results.  
The grill is relatively easy to clean, but the grease on the bottom of the bowl can build up and periodic cleaning is essential.  
So far, we are satisfied with our purchase as it is small enough to be portable in our camping trailer and eliminates the need and mess of charcoal.  It produces a lot of heat and the squirrels can't get into it with the lid closed.  For our purposes it is acceptable but it would not replace a larger multi-burner unit temperature controlled unit for general outside grilling use.

title: Good customer service, quality and product lacking
text:
Bought from local Ace Hardware as a christmas present. Was missing the char basket and screw for handle. Called weber support and got sent replacements for both with no hassle except the char basket took a couple weeks and came a week late but was getting delivered during winter storm so no complaints there. Putting together the grill was definitely a bit of a hassle and some parts aren't screwed tight and it came with a warming rack which I don't really use so it's just collecting dust in the garage. Overall I think getting the original 22 inch is definitely more worth it than the master touch. For almost 300 dollars the quality wasn't really up to my expectations and the original is about half the price and can do what the master touch can do. If you grill everyday or something I guess this would be worth it for the ash catcher, char basket, and increased height but if you're a beginner or don't grill that much I would definitely recommend getting the original. Honestly the dome thermometer also is something I don't really look at so save the money and use it to buy an actual accurate thermometer for the ambient temp. 

Sorry for the rambling but TLDR save the money and just buy the original weber 22 and mod it

My proclivity to stick with a charcoal grill was my driving force here, as I find my hubby is much more attentive to cooking with charcoal as opposed to a gas grill, though one day we might get another one of those, and you cannot beat the taste of food cooked on a charcoal grill.

The heat guard on the handle of the lid is a nice updrade and I love the grate with the option to add on different attachments like a griddle, wok, or grilling stone. title: Not what they used to be
text:
This is the third or forth Weber I  have owned. This one is obviously the result of trying to cheapen the product through foreign manufacturing. One-they have gone to one handle not two. This provides less places to hang BBQ utensils. It also makes it difficult to move if it has been recently used and is hot. Two-the lid is not as tough as in the past. My new lid slide off the back, landed in the grass and has deformed so I have to push it aggressively for it to seat to the base. (My old one hit the grass numerous times with no issues.) Three-the coating they are using is also cheaper. Where the one handle is tack welded onto the base it is rusting after two months (I got it for Christmas) My old grill is still in the edge of the yard and after nine years there is no rust at either of the two handles. Lastly-On my previous grill I could put the lid on and leave a crescent moon opening by leaving the lid ajar-it provided for another option for heat retention. This unit, if you try that the lid slides off-therefore hitting the grass and deforming the lid. It is also obvious that they are trying to hide the country of manufacture-the aluminium shield at the adjustable vent says"engineered in Palatine, IL" not manufactured in the USA. 
It is a sad epitaph to a once superior company and product.

title: PERFECT for two, EASY and FUN!
text:
When my husband went on the carnivore diet it became "too much" to clean up the stove of meat grease every meal and he suggested getting a grill.  I was intimidated by the thought of grilling every day (I'd never grilled before in my life at 52, LOL!), but the thought of a continuously clean kitchen encouraged me...and I'm SO HAPPY WE GOT IT!!!  

It's SUPER EASY to use, the perfect size for 6 1/3 lb burgers (although I usually cook 3 at a time). I LOVE the built in grill thermometer.  It helps a lot since just timing it doesn't account for ambient temperature and that does affect pre-heat and grilling times; it's winter in New England so whether it's 25 or 40 degrees outside makes a difference.

I recommend a stainless steel "fish turner" type of flipper; it's perfect for getting between the grill and the charred goodness of the burger so half of it isn't stuck.  Of course, having the grill hot enough and leaving it long enough before turning is essential, but the beveled edge of the fish spatula along with its thinness makes it almost a given that you're going to get all the yummy browned part on your plate.  Not that that's a review of the grill, just a tip.

title: Spirit E-310 Grill is superior to previous Weber's

Have had the E-310 for 6 weeks and have used at least 6 times. It is easy to start and operate.
It is similar to our prior Weber grill that was used frequently for the past 20 yrs. Hope we will enjoy this grill as long. So far the cast iron grates are easy to remove and clean. I was skeptical because prior grate was stainless tubes which were perfect. The arrangement of the burners are superior to our past grill which is a design improvement by Weber. The grease catch pan under under the burners are also a significant improvement when cleaning the grill.

title: It hasn't worked out
text: I'm having issues with the burners. Specifically, uneven heat

title: Awesome Grill
text: Awesome solid grill. Well worth the money. Very easy to put together.

title: Should have purchased a Webber years ago
text: Today  we grilled with our new Webber grill ,very impressed food was terrific ..all i can say is if you by a new grill every four years ...purchase a Webber  wont regret...

title: Don’t buy the discount units; buy the right

title: Nothing but Class
text: Very pleased with my Weber Grill. Sturdy and well built. Nothing but class from Weber!

title: Good grill for the price.
text: Very easy to put together with good instructions. Only used it once for some hamburgers, but everything worked as expected and we're sure it'll work fine for other foods as well..

title: Don't Let The Price Scare You
text: I just started using the grill and, so far, I love it.  I've always wanted a Weber but the price kept getting in the way.  At the age of 80, I finally made the investment.  Should have done it years ago.

title: Weber Grill Review

title: Why a Weber?

Only negative is loading tank somehwhat difficult. Starter is somehwhat in the way. Need to be careful not to hit it whe installing tank.

title: Overpriced Weber grill cover
text: I love the size of this grill. I replaced the III. But the grill cover at $80 is actually insulting. Seriously. So for this reason, I give the brand a thumbs down..

title: Great Grill
text: Great.  This grill is awesome.  Easy to clean, cooks evenly and small enough to store in our RV.

title: Back to charcoal.
text: Great grill, solid construction and very friendly, awesome purchase.

title: Best compact grill on the market. Good price.
text: This is my second Q1200 series grill. The first one lasted 10+ years. I recently moved and gave it to my neighbor. I bought a new one last month. Cooks as good as any grill on the market.

title: Love it.
text: I've always used cheaper grills because the inside just seems to rot away and I thought Weber was similar. I think I'm wrong about that. This grill is really solid and cooks evenly. I guess time will tell about how long it lasts but I love it after 6 uses. I definitely recommend it. The 2 burner one is more than big enough for 2 of us and is actually bigger than 3 burner grills I've had.

title: The best!
text: Very happy i made my purchase! Ive always been a charcoal guy and i learned from my dad longago that the Weber Kettle is the waynto go! Its been awhile since ive owned one due but no regrets! Nothing beats the smell of the briquettes and an open flame!

title: quality product
text: This is a well built and thought out grill.  It is the perfect size.  I think 2 burner grills sometimes fail to heat up enough for the size of the box but this is three burner and heats up nicely.  Unless you regularly grill for 6 or more this is all the space you need.  Very good quality grill...buy it.

title: Spirit II E-210
text: Well made, worth the price paid, better than the others I have owned.

title: What to Say?  It's a Weber
text: Sturdy, efficient, even heat distribution, and, once assembled, the quickest and cleanest way to grill.  I bought this to replace an old Weber Spirit III which lasted almost 20 years.  There's a reason that Weber has the reputation it does.  Clean your grill after every use, and cover it to protect it from inclement weather (and to provide shelter for mice!).  Easy to assemble and with the right maintenance, will outlast most other models.

title: Perfect grill
text: First time owning a Weber. Perfect grill! Would definitely purchase again!

title: Great grilling
text: Can regulate temp my self,can also cook with indirect heat or sear without any electronics malfunctioning to mess up my meat,  I like being involved in my cooking. Got rid of a pellet smoker and grill went back to weber,thank you weber.

title: Great Tasting
text: This is our 3rd Weber propane grill and we’ve enjoyed them all. They’re designed well, cook great and hold up over time.

title: The most bang for your buck
text: Quality product    Affordable and well made   I will continue to buy Weber products

title: Awesome
text: Does exactly what they say it supposed to. Wonderful grill👍

title: Igniter
text: Requested a replacement solenoid for igniter.  Received and igniter is now working.

title: Is Weber worth it?
text: I bought my Weber spirit II on February 2024. I used it twice before it failed to ignite. Ever since, I have been working with a customer service group of people who try their best to rid themselves of my problem without resolving it. They refuse to let me speak to a supervisor. I’m forwarding my complaint to corporate for resolution

title: You get what you pay for.
text: Weber support helped send a part that was initially incorrectly packaged - the back panel. The Spirit E-310 is a quality product that reinforced the statement "you get what you pay for."

title: Second Weber Grill ❣️
text: This is our second Weber grill. Really like them!!

title: Latest in a long line of Weber grills
text: This replaces a Spirit 700 grill that I bought about 20 years ago (the copyright on the manual is 2001). Rust finally got to it. The new one is not as heavy and I'm not sure this one will last as long, but it works well and it's the right size for us. I think if I keep it clean and covered it'll be around for a while. I had Weber's smoker and I have a Weber charcoal grill. Take care of them and they'll last.

title: Spirit Ii 3 burner
text: I really am impressed with initial heat up and consistent retention of heat settings. And indirect cooking has worked well for two dinners of pork ribs.

title: Campers delite !
text: Awesome camping grill very versatle in cooking with the griddle.Grills steaks to perfection in very little time.

title: Old Webber Was Good, New One Is Great
text: I owned a Webber Grill for 35 years and replaced it in March with a E-210 Gas Grill.  I don't know why I waited so long.  I use my grill about 5 times or more a week, in snow, rain, or sunshine. It is on my deck and ready to use when I want. I am 73 years old and like the easy to use E-210 Gas Grill by Webber.

title: Webet will not stand behind their warranty
text: I have two spirit grills they have performed well up until I needed warranty work. The sticker with the warranty number and serial number is directly below the grease catch. The grease had washed away the number and since I did not have the serial number they would not honor the warranty even though I sent them pictures proving I had two of them. I will never buy another Weber product until they take care of this problem

title: Overall amazing customer service
text: I had a situation that needed customer service attention. They were quick to help and my Weber experience has been more than a 5 star rating. They went above and beyond to make sure I had a product that I can enjoy years to come …..

title: Great Grill
text: works great, I have wanted a weber grill for a long time.  I don't know why I waited so long.

title: Weber 1200 with cart.
text: I love my Weber 1200. Easy size to use and travel with. Pretty colors too. I got red. Very nice.

title: My new Weber grill
text: Good grill for the money.  Heats up quickly and cools down just as fast

title: love my Weber
text: Priced right , smaller footprint but perfect size for 2 people yet big enough for a small party . 3 burners means plenty of heat. Love my Weber only issue Ihave is the crazy amount of cardboard that Ihad to shred up to get in my recycling bin, I understand Weber is protecting the product but maybe someone should look into this .

title: Not my first Weber!
text: Love the quality of Weber…..we have loved, bought and used Weber kettles for at least 30 years. Excellent value, exceptional quality, the best grilling experience you could want. When we get a new kettle, we pass our old one to a new user…..

title: Think Twice, poor LPG tank setup
text:
Nice Grill, I’m a big fan of indirect cooking and even with only 2 burners this works well.
There is 1 really big issue though and that is with the tank holder and gas hookup. As others have stated, it is very difficult to lift the tank high enough to rest on the fuel guage and then the way the tanks are configured you have to turn the tank to hook it onto the fuel guage and this puts stress on the gas to grill connection. This connection has loosened on its own causing leaks. The cabinet needs to be larger or the hose needs to be longer.

title: Nice Grill So Far
text: So far, so good...no signs of early corrosion as has been mentioned in other reviews, but, it's only been exposed to the elements for a month or two, and covered. BTW, the grill cover protects from the weather superbly...it's a bit on the pricey side, but IMO, worth it...well constructed, as expected with anything branded by Weber. Will update this review later on if corrosion begins to turn up prematurely. The grill functions flawlessly...and couldn't be happier.

title: Love Weber Spirit Grills!
text: Our 3rd Weber grill!  The last gas Weber Spirit with 2 burners lasted 10 years with little maintenance.

title: Love the New Grill
text:
Its a great grill..pricey but worth it!
Lowes assembly and delivered to my Deck! Wow
Good job for a 60 yr old lady unable to do that!
My food is cooking wonderfully. 
The ignite is dependable.. it just looks great.
I bought a cheaper cover from lowes fits fine.
Im really enjoying it!  Happy Grilling!

title: Topless!
text: Sturdy and well built.  Have only grilled a few times since we got it, but the food has been good. Have to be sure not to overcook and dry out the food.  One complaint is that when you buy a grill that is this expensive, it should come with a grill cover and not be topless!

title: Great investment!
text: Very pleased. Best grill I ever owned. Versatile and easy to use.

title: No instructions on how to clean grates
text: I am enjoying the grill, but I have one complaint. The instructions that come with the grill do not cover how to properly clean the grates. I had to go to the internet. There I was told "never put the grates in the dishwasher." No such warning came with the grill. Unfortunately, I had already done so in preparation for using it. I hope no damage has occurred. I would much prefer to have advice from you as the manufacturer than searching the internet.

title: Cheap stainless steel.
text: Grill works fine.  2 things:  (1)  Even though I use your grill cover there are beginnings of rust streaks on the 2 side arms. Your Customer Service rep sent me (gratis) your stainless steel polish which didn't cover/move any of it.  (2)  Not having a man on the premises it wasa impossible to lift the propane container on your gauge.  Surprise!

title: First Weber
text: I always thought char broil was a great grill ,and it is ,but I am really enjoying my first Weber.

title: Perfect for a party of two or up to six.
text: We love this grill. Not too big, not too small for our needs. Heat is even, grilling is easy.

title: Cooks food fast and hot
text: Cooks food Hotter and Faster then any grill I've had

title: Smaller unit does a big job
text: Great size for a gathering or small group.  Quality is very good, and cooks evenly.  Solid product

title: Good bbq
text: I am very happy with this grill it has everything a charcoal bbq needs.  A thumbs up

title: Webber warranty
text: I bought my grill 3 years ago. This is my 3rd webber grill. One of the burners stopped working . I couldn't fund my receipt . I called webber and explained the issue. They troubleshoot the problem and sent me the parts free of charge. Incredible that they honored the warranty. I am so happy my grill is working again.

title: Perfect Grill for our RV
text: We purchased this grill for our RV due to it size and ability to be converted to connect to our RV propane system.  The kit is sold separately on Amazon comes with all hardware and 12ft hose.    This grill is shipped with a regulator for use with small propane bottles. If you’re doing the conversion the regulator is removed. The construction and quality of the grill is typical Weber, excellent.  The grates are heavy and the surface is of sufficient size to cook 6-8 burgers.  It’s is easy to clean and store.  We’re very happy with it and use it often.

title: Quality
text: Weber has a good reputation for quality products; my new Weber bears this out. The frame is sturdy, and the internal parts are solid and nicely finished.

title: Open cart better than cabinet design
text: Looked at Weber grills for 2 years. Finally found they were on sale for $50.00 off. Nice grill. Lots of parts to put together. Only grilled a couple of times on it. Seems to be a great grill. I did a lot of research on all the Webers before picking this one. I like it better than the cabinet design and don't think it will rust as easy since it only has the 2 legs touching the deck. Also no big "lip" like on the cabinet design.

title: Lots of love for the charcoal grill
text: I am very happy with the Master Touch grill.  It assembled easily and is a solid unit.  I especially like the cleaning system and the ash catcher.  Have used it for indirect cooking three times and have not been disappointed at all.  Love it!

title: Spirit Ii E -310 with half griddle
text: Well worth the money.  I also purchased the half griddle and use the combo daily.  I would recommend as this cooks like a champ.

title: Side Table issue
text: I paid more for this grill than any other grill I've previously owned. To move the grill you pick up the side table to roll.What a cheaply made flimsy piece to pick up on and roll.So flimsy that when it came off it bent it all up.The grill works great. Was looking forward to owning my first weber grill but disappointed in the quality of it.I don't know if i would buy another one.

title: Finally on sale, I didn’t hesitate!!
text:
My Genesis lasted 15+ years, with multiple updates to the inner components (rust takes a toll). It did great to the end, but alas, the inner box structure was going. I saw this Spirit on sale at Lowe’s and went for it (over $100 off).
It has 3 burner configuration where my old one was in a U shape around the front, side and back. This is much better and I can control each burner bar! Love it. Thanks!

title: This is a really good grill.
text: Weber Grills are excellent values. They cook well and stand up to high usage and tough weather conditions.  It’s also easy to find replacement parts when needed.

title: Tiny grill
text:
It’s a tiny grill .   I have no idea why people think these are so great!  You can barely fit meat on it much less any thing else.
I used it once and returned it.
Don’t waste your money.

title: Inferior parts
text: The wheels rotted out before the warranty. Replacing the wheels have been a nightmare and who wants to spend money on the same wheels that will rot out in less than 5 years. Igniter is in poor location, it is hit with tank with installation of tank every time, gave up in replacing it.

title: Best grill ever!!!!
text: Weber spirt II propane outdoor grill is the best, heats up fast, grills evenly, easy to clean, sturdy frame, built well. We bought our first 6 years ago that we have at our cabin in Maine which is still cooking as good as day we purchased. Now we purchased our second one to replace “other brand” grill at home that was terrible. New one was still as great as our first. Truly great grill!!!

title: Love Our Grill!
text: This grill is perfect for our small family. We love it!

title: The perfect size
text: I have always grilled on a Weber. Had a 4 burner and then a 2 burner and have finally arrived at the 3 burner. I am slow but I am sure. It allows me the flexibility I need without the size. Exterior tank was a must.  Not as strong as I used to be.

title: Awesome!
text: Exceeded our expectations. Weber has thought of everything. Easy to clean, drain pan, fill tank, etc. Best grill!

title: Disappointed
text: Cools off to quickly, also disappointed in warming tray not being connected.

title: Could not start grill.
text: Customer service was outstanding.  They walked through with me to troubleshoot the problem of not starting.  They identified the problem and rectified it by resupplying me with a new regulator.

title: First Weber
text: Best grill! It’s our first Weber and it hasn’t disappointed yet.

title: Compact design, performs great
text: Compact but ample cooking area.  Simple cleaning.  Cooks great even in chilly or windy weather.  Gas tank gauge is great, shows when gas is running low to avoid surprises.  Should have purchased this over our last Char Broil setup.

title: Love it
text: This is our 2nd Weber and we love it. They last and grill great.

title: Good, and almost great
text: The provided part fixed the issue I was having.  The only reason for the four stars was or is due to hotspots on the cooking areas.  A griddle may help fix this issue

title: Grill Master
text: I recently purchased the Weber Spirit E-210. I really enjoy using this grill. I like that it is the right size for my grilling. The sides fold and the propane tank is hidden. I also can lock the wheels from moving. This product is so great. By the way,my former grill was the Weber Spirit E-210.

title: We love our Weber !!
text: It's perfect for our beach house. We needed a new grill for our summer home, but we wanted a more compact one since it would be used on a second-floor balcony.   We love it !! I had to get used to the heat settings as this grill heats up very fast and holds the temperature like no other grill I have had over my 54 years.  I purchased this E-210 based on reviews, and the other 5-star reviews were spot on. Great job Weber, this grill is a keeper.

title: loves my weber
text: i actually won this grill ,but it replaced my weber gas grille that was 5 years old and still in great shape so i gave it to my daughter, she should get another 5 out of it, its the only grill that will hold up

title: Best present ever from my daughter.
text: I upgraded my grill this year to the classic Weber kettle grill and I couldn’t be happier with it.

title: Quality product
text: Once you own a Weber, you know. No other brand will do. This one is our second Weber. We owned our first one for 27 years. We never covered it, it sat out in the rain. We replaced the burners twice. The tabs supporting the drip tray finally gave way which is why we bought a new grill, same size etc as the old one. Couldn’t be happier. The new grill heats faster and is more efficient than the old one! We love it, worth every penny.

title: Wonderful!
text: Easy to use.  Easy to clean.  Great for grilling and smoking.

title: Weber Master Touch grill review
text: The Weber Master Touch Kettle Grill has exceeded my expectations so far with it's versatile design and Exceptional performance. from a wonderfully seared steak to slow cooked stuffed chicken. this has been a very enjoyable grill so far. I had an issue with the top handle when I bought it the warranty department handled wonderfully with out question and sent me a brand new handle. the durable construction and ease of use will give me many more years or grilling pleasure before I have to replace this unit.

title: Always will be the Goat
text: Nothing will ever cook as good as a weber kettle.  Grill, BBQ, and smoke all on this.

title: Great little grill!
text:
I'm so glad my husband picked out this Weber grill. It's small size, but perfect for the two of us. In the summer, using our oven really heats up our home. So we're using this grill as our main source for cooking. You can cook practically everything on there. Our Weber Spirit II 
E-210 gas grill is definitely one of our smartest purchases. If you're looking for a grill, I'd say go Weber. You won't go wrong.

title: Great kettle barbecue
text: I own a pellet smoker. After using the Weber kettle I prefer using the Webber. I get much better flavor from the Weber kettle barbecue

title: We downsized, but enjoy the grill.
text: This unit is just the right size for us. It is easy to use and to maintain.

title: Quality
text: Overall the grill does a good job. Disappointed by the quality. Owned a silver series Weber for 17 years and the quality was much higher vs this one.

title: Hook inside cover

title: Happy guy
text: I have used it three times so far and steaks and burgers have been great

title: Great gas grill
text: A great compact grill which heats up quickly and very hot. Love it.

title: Best Grill Ever
text: Another great product from Weber. My first gas grill and I kept my Kettle that is over 30 years old. Finally replaced the bottom grate. Nice to have a choice or use both for parties.

title: Perfect grill for a small family or limited space
text: Can't say enough about this grill. Picked it up as a floor model special from the store that rhymes with Owe's. Even heating over the whole grill surface, and great temp control. It could benefit from a slightly bigger warming rack, and better design of the grill tool "hooks" ( the hooks aren't really useful at all), but that's about it. I like the extra storage space underneath, and it's easy to get the grease traps out for cleaning. Bigger than the 210, which would be fine for a really small space, but not as bulky as the larger models. Perfect fit for me.

title: Nice Grill
text: I love the grill. It's well built and solid. The only negative is that where they placed the propane tank is hard to use. The permanent shelf on top is always in the way when I want to replace the tank. There is very little room under that shelf to lift and set a very heavy 20 # tank. I really struggle when I have to replace the tank.

title: Great Grill
text: Weber never disappoints! I purchased this grill because I love the taste of charcoal grilled food. I know it takes longer, but it’s worth it in the end when it comes down to taste. I also used charcoal briquettes to slowly smoke some ribs. It took 6 hours for 2 racks of St Louis style ribs and the taste was fantastic! The new lid design was also helpful because I didn’t have to find somewhere to lay the lid while checking on the food

title: Weber grills forever
text: I bought the E-210 to replace  my  20 year old weber. It's small enough for my deck and big enough to handle having a few friends over. I even fire it up for just the wife and I. It is easy to clean. I am looking forward to many years of service from this grill.

title: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)
text: This grill does a fantastic job.  It is easy to clean and the tank designed for the outside is a real advantage for anyone who has to change it.  I never understood why they designed it for the  inside in the first place.  It cooks everything beautifully. Very pleased with our choice!

title: Not worth the cost, only a 2 year warranty!
text: Not worth the money, burner valve failed at 3 years, grill only has 2 year warranty. So expect to have to buy more Chinese parts from them after purchase. Almost 200 dollars quoted from Weber to replace burner valve a knob that got stripped because of failed burner valve and the igniter that broke. I did purchase aftermarket burner valve on Amazon for much cheaper and fixed my problem but for a grill that cost over 500 bucks you would expect it to last a lot longer. I thought the Weber name meant quality. Should have bought a cheaper grill and expected things to fail.

title: Best Grill I’ve had!
text: Best Grill I’ve had! Love the temp control. Heavy duty and very sturdy. Propane indicator is very handy. Easy to clean.

title: Perfect
text:
I Am very satisfied with the Spirit II perfect size for just me in the house and even if a few friends stop by   .if i had any friends LOL.
It was super easy to build  great directions.

title: Not the Weber qualify I expected
text: Grill arrived with damaged legs. Getting replacement legs was very difficult and took longer than I anticipated. Partially due to Customer support and forcing you to work with a virtual agent. Once new legs arrived they did not fit as shown. So frustrated, I returned it!

title: Completely Satisfied
text: I purchase this Weber for camping and picnics. I've had a three burner Webner for several years and so well pleased with it that led me to purchase another Webner. Fully satisfied with the how well it is built and except for the difference in size, the same as my bigger grill.

title: Consistent Kettle Cooker
text: This is a good grill as the shape makes for even cooking and temperatures for both direct and indirect cooking. It is very simple to use and sturdy enough to last for years. It does have replacement parts which I have also purchased to keep the cooking going.

title: A DUD
text: Got 2 years ago for a vacation home. Used a total of less than 50 times

title: Easy to start up
text:
Really like the new (to me) ignition system. So simple tp light and seems to work very well.
It is much lighter in weight than my old Genesis grill, will have to wait to judge that.

title: Perfect grill for small and large meals.
text: This is my second E-210. I used the first one until the wheels actually fell off. It's the perfect small size for just me and big enough to hold a lot more food when i have company.  Grill temperature is good and adjusts quickly if needed.

title: High Quality Grill
text: The Weber Spirit E-310 is a well-made, quality grill with very accurate temperature control.  I appreciate the ruggedness of the design and materials.  There are some nice innovative features such as a fuel gauge for your propane tank and an improved ignition system.   I truly enjoy it and use it multiple times weekly.   Great product - great value!

title: Weber
text: This model Spirit Weber 3 burner grill, is just the right size for what we need it to do. Works great, and we are happy with the purchase.

title: Weber is my grill of choice
text:
I’m a diehard believer in Weber products.
I have owned a Weber grill since I was 18 and I’m in my sixties now.
This is a very nice portable LP grill that still preforms like a standard full size grill with great heat retention and flavour while having the mobility of a tabletop unit.
I’m looking forward to summer and grilling season ,even though I grill year around.
Cheers!
Steve Johnson

title: Great Quality and Performance!!
text: I bought my Spirit 210 five years ago, and it still works fantastic! The only thing I have had to replace is the heat shields, a normal wear item. I highly recommend this grill.

title: Very good mid-size grill.
text: Purchased as a replacement for the Weber Genesis I used for the past dozen years.  Good searing capability with the three burners and enough control for indirect cooking.  An excellent choice when cooking for 1-4 people.  Typical high quality Weber materials and construction.

title: Customer Service has fallen off dramatically.
text: I have a Weber genesis and decided to purchase a charcoal grill mostly for nostalgias sake.  I’ve used it handful of times already and the grill itself is wonderful, however, Customer Service has fallen off dramatically since I bought my genesis about seven Years ago.  When I bought my genesis and unboxed it, there was a chip in the porcelain by the thermometer, and I called and spoke to someone who was extremely knowledgeable and immediately sent a replacement and he even sent me a grill cover for the inconvenience free of charge.  With my master, for whatever reason, it did not come with the charcoal baskets that I had seen in every review and every Master touch assemble YouTube videos I’ve seen. I called and spoke to two separate people who didn’t even know what a charcoal basket was and were zero help, and I finally spoke to a third person who finally had a clue and he said that yes they were in fact supposed to come with charcoal baskets, and he would send them out right away. A week later I got a single charcoal basket….  It has been very frustrating.  Weber has outsourced their customer service, Which was not the case years ago.

title: Second time around
text: This is actually our second Weber grill.  The first one lasted 15 years. This new grill is very easy to use. It lit right up, the cooking grates worked like a charm.

title: Build quality,  performane, and warranty.
text: I bought because of build quality, warranty, and performance.  Weber delivers on all. Sure you pay more but you get so much more. I have had cheaper grills in the past but after 5 years they needed to be replaced. I have no doubts that this grill will last easily 10 years and more. I bought the E210 because of the size. I live in a condo and it was the best option for my balcony.

I would give this grill 5 stars if Weber sold stainless steel grates for this model.  The only drawback for me is the cleaning of the porcelain cast grates.  Stainless would be much easier to clean.  I've had this grill for over 15 years and it still works beautifully.  Its small size is appropriate for our family and fits in a nook on our deck.  The local business that sold this to me has given me good service over the years.

title: Good Grill, Minor Glitch
text: I've had Weber Kettles before and they work great for grilling. My only concern with my latest purchase is that the hook under the lid for hanging the lid on the side of the grill is a bit small. It is harder to engage with the edge of the grill than I remember from my older grills. I almost dropped the lid on the concrete patio once when the small hook failed to reach the grill. I'd like to see the hook at least 1/2 inch longer.

title: Great little grill
text: Great little grill - so easy and cooks perfectly every time.

title: Excellent grill
text: Love my grill. Easy to use, clean and so easy to use!!!!

title: Third Weber grill
text: My third Weber grill, still the best made of any I owned in the past.

title: Weber's great continuation of reliable service
text: Easy to operate, looks great didn't have any problem with first use.

title: Spirit ll LP grill
text: So far, we have enjoyed using our Spirit ll Gas Grill. It's small so it doesn't take up too much space on our porch, but big enough to grill most any meat we choose to cook. It controls the heat as well as most grills we have owned. Highly recommend getting a Weber grill.

title: Great grill, but out of square frame.

text:

The tilt up cover is OK but makes working the grill with standard restaurant tongs and the lid hinged up is another hand burner. The lid up reflects heat back to the cooking surface. 
The heavier grate material is a plus but I'm not sure it's different enough from the Original Premium kettle at $220. Same goes for the larger wheels. 
The ash catcher is a nice design improvement but it's also on the Original Premium kettle.

My Bottom Line.. Save $55 and buy the Original Premium 22" Grill.

title: What a Difference $200 Makes!
text:
We got the Weber Spirit E-210 Gas Grill several weeks ago and have used it extensively for grilling bratwurst, steaks, hamburgers, corn, vegetables, barbecued ribs--you name it. It has met our expectations in every respect. My impressions as follows:

THE GOOD

The grill is solidly built. The title of this review ($200) refers to a gas grill of a different make but similar size purchased by my daughter awhile back. She paid about $200 less for hers than we paid for ours, but the difference in build quality is huge! Hers, while it functions well, is primarily thin sheet metal construction. The Spirit E-210 is solid. I estimate that it is at least twice as heavy as hers and is obviously built to last. This holds true for cooking and burner surfaces as well: solidly made and heavy. Oh--just a quick mention. I spent half a day assembling my daughter's grill. We purchased ours already assembled--AND Ace Hardware helped us load it. 

It is compact. One of the criteria for us (retired couple living in Florida) was a grill small enough to be accommodated in a limited space. The Spirit E-210 has inside propane tank storage and side table flaps that fold down for storage. When not in use it occupies a space just a little over 2' x 2' x 3.5' tall, fitting nicely into a corner of our lanai.

It heats fast and evenly--no apparent "cool" areas once it was heated and ready to cook. It was amazing to watch the temp. gauge rise once we turned it on with both burners on high: the needle was close to the 600 degree mark in just a few minutes. The solid build of the unit, especially the cover which sits solidly on the frame, helps keep heat in instead of radiating a lot of it away. Additionally the burners are responsive: it can cook "low and slow" for ribs, or hot enough to produce a medium NY Strip Steak in less than 9 minutes. The indirect heat is nice as well. Though it gets very hot, no flame ever contacts the food (though grease flares will happen).

THE BAD

Well, maybe "The Not Quite Up To Expectations" would be a better title for this section, because there is nothing really bad about this unit. But...

The casters, while totally functional, seem a bit small for the unit. It is a heavy unit and casters possibly a bit bigger would be a big help rolling it over uneven surfaces, or in and out of our lanai. We have to lift up the end being rolled over the threshold--a minor annoyance, but still there. 

Another condition larger casters would help alleviate is that the wheel brakes on the unit (each front caster has a toe brake which can be set so the unit doesn't roll accidentally), can only be set with the front wheels at near 90 degrees to the unit. If not, the brake lever cannot be reached with a toe and we have to reach under the unit to adjust the wheel to the correct position. 

The warming rack, while perfectly usable, is a bit small. Maybe 6" wider would increase its functionality.

The gas bottle rides on a clip inside the unit that also functions as a measuring device to tell you how much gas is left. I've never used (or even seen) one of those before so I am just a little nervous about it...like a solution for which there is no problem. But hey! Maybe it is great. Time will tell.

THE UGLY

There ain't no ugly!

THE BOTTOM LINE

Frankly, so far this grill has exceeded our expectations...and we expected a lot! Obviously we cannot assess its longevity at this point but the good design and heavy build quality leaves little room for doubt that it will shine in that area as well. I'd certainly recommend it.

title: GOOD LOOKS, GREAT HEAT CONTROL & FRIENDLY DESIGN
text:
So far, I really like my Spirit II E-210 LP Gas grill. I’ve followed manual suggestion to allow for a 10-min preheating with gas set on max gas flow. This has worked great as temperature is sufficiently high for a great sear on steaks, burgers, etc. 

From a design standpoint, I love the lack of sharp edges or corners on the side shelves. Most grills I’ve owned had sharply squared off edges. These present almost guaranteed spots to rip grill covers, especially during winter seasons where the cold weather tends to make grill covers less flexible, and therefore prone to tears. The Spirit II has rounded, smooth plastic corners which should go a long way to prevent tears. 

I have a feeling that I’m going to get a lot of excellent use from this grill for a very long time.

title: A Great Entry to the Weber Grill Ecosystem
text:
I purchased this grill for myself as a birthday present (after a little gas-or-pellet grill debating) and I'm certainly glad I did. Easily the most even cooking grill I've ever owned. Heats up quickly to any temp I've needed so far and everything has been flavorful and beautiful (great sear marks!) 

It took me a little over an hour to assemble after taking 30 minutes or so to just lay out all the pieces. It's a sturdy unit and, even though there were numerous steps to the assembly process, it went together easily. I can say two people working together should be able to knock this out in 45 minutes or so. I also appreciate the way the packaging was done, very tidy, no dings or dents to any of the parts.

I'm a bit of a no bells and whistles guy when it comes to grilling, so even though the Genesis grills were a bit of a temptation, nobody should hesitate for a minute in purchasing the E-310. Those who are looking at the Spirit E-310 and the Spirit II E-310, just bear in mind a couple of things. The Spirit II (this grill) uses the G4 grilling system (grease pan in the middle, not offset to one side) and the Spirit II is the one that is OPEN underneath. Aesthetically for me, I like the more rugged looks of the Spirit II version of the E-310 but either grill should be fine. But, if you're like me and you need a reliable, easy-to-use gas grill (LP for me) for burgers, brats, chicken, steak, etc., I can say without a doubt the Spirit II E-310 will be a great choice!

title: Nothing rewards like quality
text:
I had purchased an Oklahoma Joe Tahoma 900, thinking it would get hot enough to be able to do both my grilling and smoking. And it can, but it is not really designed for that, and you go through a ton of charcoal to get it up to 500 degrees.

I had a weber spirit 3 burner before that I used lovingly for 10 years, but eventually it just was getting too hard to keep up and there was some rust, etc... 

Sooooo... I did a week's worth of research on getting a cheap gas grill for my weekday grilling (I grill something 3 or 4 nights a week) that is simple. Light it, wait until its hot and grill it.
I went to multiple stores (Lowes, Home Depot, Menards, Ace Hardware) and checked out the 'cheap' ones, and lets just say you get what you pay for. Some were okay, but I could tell they would be falling apart in a couple years. 

So, my recommendation is pay up for the quality. The weber E-210 is almost the perfect small deck/patio grill. Assembly was a little hard for my 60 year-old knees, but wasn't particularly hard (note: put something down underneath on a deck... I lost 2 screws that fell through the deck and had to go to the hardware store to replace). It lit and fired up the first time. I already have a Bluetooth remote meat probe, so no need to pay extra for the built in ones. 

Also, I liked that the propane tank hangs on the side with easy access. With my old Weber, it had a cabinet underneath (that was useless and just collected dirt and grime) and bending over with a heavy propane tank  and hanging it inside the cabinet was a pain. 

Two burners is more than enough for a family of 4 and you can be eating at the table in same time it takes to pre-heat a pellet grill or charcoal. Trust me... I've used them all.

title: Huge Step Up From A Portable Gas Grill
text:
I went 10-years without a full-sized propane grill after moving.  We started camping not long after the move, so I used my portable camping grill (from another brand) both at home and while camping.  Two years ago we bought a vacation property and got a Spirit II E-210 to use there.  It was a great choice because of the extra space, two burners, and moving away from 1-lb propane cannisters.  Heat is consistent and adjustable.  I also appreciate the larger wheels for moving the grill and the ability to fold down the left side table. The spring actuated propane gauge has worked well enough to keep me from running out while grilling.

This year we decided to upgrade our home grilling abilities and I looked to Weber again.  I considered the Spirit EX-315 at a membership store, but ruled it out because of the electronic temperature gauge and small wheels.  After ruling out that bigger model, it made sense to get the same Spirit II E210 as we have at our other place. It will be easy to switch back and forth between operating the two grills.

I'm giving this grill only 3-stars, and here's why.  First, almost all of the best in-grill accessories from Weber are made for the 300-series grills and above.  Second, two burners are not ideal for indirect cooking.  Third, Weber took out the iGrill feature to save money but didn't spend the money to print a 200-series user manual that doesn't reference this feature.  Fourth, this new grill runs at least 100-degrees hotter than our original grill of the same model.   And finally, the influence Weber has over the sales channels can create a poor purchasing experience.  I had multiple options and went with a locally owned franchise hardware store who a) assembled the fuel gauge wrong, and b) were very reluctant to address a pricing promotion that started very shortly after my purchase.

The problem was the flame was not adjustable and I couldn't get any heat out of it to cook. It was well past Amazon return window so I called Weber and the very first person I talked with was very nice person and he walked me through some steps and then told me he would send a free regulator and it would take up to two weeks to receive it. I received a fuel hose in stead of the regulator.I called Weber back and the person that I talked with again was very nice person and he said he would send me the regulator but again that would take up to 2 weeks. I received the regulator but you need a special tool to get the regulator off, finally got one at home depot. So between the fixed ratchet and the very short screw driver I still cannot get the regulator off!! I asked a handyman for help and he was going to charge me $100. 
I am a widowed 71yo women on a fixed income and cannot afford to buy a new bbq this year. I am in tears this will be the first time in over 35 years that I won't have a bbq.

title: The OG of Kettle Grills
text:
A Weber kettle was my first charcoal grill (talking early ‘80s), and it was a solid cooking partner for many years until I finally replaced it with a Brinkman. After some 25 years on that grill, I “upgraded” to a Char Griller offset smoker. Big mistake, as it wasn’t able to a) handle the heat from a wood fire and b) was frustrating to use as a direct charcoal grill due to the decreased distance between the fire and the food. By then, Brinkman was no mas, and I was stuck.

Ultimately it was decided that the smoking was going to happen on a Yoder pellet grill, and the food that really shines when cooked over charcoal was gonna happen on a new Weber.

Gotta hand it to Weber, they didn’t mess too much with what was already working. I appreciate the heat shield underneath the handle on the lid, and the temperature gauge is also a welcome addition. Get the Premium though, so you’ll have that handy ash clean out. It’s a safety issue really, since it helps prevent hot ashes/tiny bits of glowing coal from blowing around. Easy to disengage and empty, and you’ll only have to do that every 3 cooks or so.

The lid still sits nice and snug on the kettle’s bottom, so you can close things up when you’re done and the fire suffocates quickly (very handy for conserving charcoal). I also love the two hinged sections of the cooking grate, so you can add more fuel without having to lift the grate/food out of the way.

If I could change one thing, it would be the orientation of the under-lid hook to 0° from the handle as opposed to its current 90°. I’m used to it now, but it does pose a greater risk of skin-to-hot lid contact. The plastic grips attached to the handles do a good job of dissipating heat, but time will tell if they hold up like their hardwood predecessors. The wheels roll well and while also made of plastic, they’re not getting hit with the heat from the kettle.

When this grill isn’t in use I cover it with a Weber cover. A pretty janky cover, in direct contrast to the awesome kettle grill. It’s too short to adequately cover those plastic wheels and a little too roomy, with only a single Velcro loop to secure it. Any kind of wind causes it to loft right off. The material itself seems cheap, too. When it goes down I’ll shop around for something more substantial for sure.

Even though it’s a full-size grill, with the side tables folded down, it fits great on my small deck.  I purchased the cover for it so that I can keep it looking like new for years to come.

title: Best Ever!!

title: Great grill with features you’ll love!
text: This grill is great and I particularly love the propane tank fuel level indicator which is standard on this grill and even on the smaller version. The tank hangs of a small scale inside the BBQ and the indicator will move as the level of fuel is consumed. The heat control is good and the space of the grill is perfect for a small to medium size deck. The quality of the product is good and was easy to assemble so don’t pay to have this done. Overall I give it 9 stars out of 10 as it is a bit more expensive than other grills of similar quality and size.

title: A nice little grill
text: This is my third Weber Propane grill, and it replaces a seventeen year old three burner Spirit Grill that still worked, but the cabinet floor had rusted away.  The new grill gets plenty hot. So don’t worry that it has just two burners.  It can easily handle eight quarter pounders or chicken breasts, or four strip steaks at two different heat levels.  It a bit pricy, but worth it.  Also, I don’t expect rust problems with it, and as with the previous Webers, I know I can get excellent product support and replacement  parts as needed.

title: New Upgraded Weber Kettle!
text:
I just moved to a new city and my old Weber Kettle didn't make the move (I forgot to tell the movers) so I decided to replace it. As I was looking over Amazon, I found the grill that I'd already had and then I saw this one with the much better system for dealing with the inevitable ash mess and didn't even think about it, I just pulled the proverbial trigger. 

It's been well over 100 degrees here pretty much since the grill arrived and it just felt like it was too hot to grill but when the temp came down to the low 90s on Saturday, I broke out the Rapid Fire Chimney, my mesquite lump charcoal and Fire Starter cubes and proceded to grill myself a USDA Prime NY Strip, rare and it was perfect! 

Thank you Weber for, once again, providing me with a great tool to make great food!

title: BBQ 24/7
text: I couldn’t be happier with my Spirit E-310 Propane Grill. This grill has everything that I was looking for. From the enclosed easy access tank location to the super heavy duty cast iron grill plates to the 3 very controllable burners. I swore up and down that I would never buy a propane grill because I have always cooked on a Weber Kettle grill using mesquite coals and If it ain’t broke why fix it. I finally had to give in though, I live in the San Bernardino County Mountains Community of Crestline and my wonderful neighbors like calling the Fire Department every time I would light up my Weber Kettle Grill because of the smoke that the coals give off would trigger a freak out from my neighbors. So I gave in and purchased a Weber propane grill and now I am bbq’ing all hours of the morning, day and night and my neighbors only get to enjoy the wonder smell of cooking meat and the S.B. County Fire Department is no longer coming out to my house. It really is nice to just last minute decide to bbq burgers and not have to hassle with the lengthy time of waiting for my coals to be ready to cook on or have to drive down the mountain to a 24 hour Walmart at 10 pm just so I can bbq and enjoy the midnight sky. This grill sips the propane giving many many cooks before a tank refill. Best decision I ever made, definitely 2 thumbs up.

title: Two issues result in loss of two stars on rating.
text: Two obvious issues:  Most obvious appears when even a light wind blows ashes out of the ash catcher dish!  The solution was to purchase and install a large capacity ash catcher # 65143.  Another minor irritation was having to wear a glove to adjust the hot lid damper.  Only solution was to purchase a # 63070 damper kit and remove the nylon handle, then install it on the original damper. Handle alone did not appear to be available for purchase, but it should be factory installed on the damper during assembly...Hot damper is a very obvious safety matter.  After adding these two features to the grill I am very pleased with it.

The size of the grill is also optimum for us as we are empty nesters, but it is large enough to cook for a few guests.  I like the folding side table and it would be ok if both folded.  If I could wish for one thing for the grill it would be that it got hotter.  A grill I had some years ago had something called sear burners on the right side of the grill and was great for steaks, which I cook frequently.  This grill is only about a month old so I cannot comment on durability yet but this is something other Weber users have cited as a strong point.

text: Seriously, I do not know why it took 57 years to purchase a Weber gas grill. Additionally, I could never figure out why I was never consistent with the quality of grilling results.  It seemed those who had a Weber grill had juicer,,more tender and aesthetically appealing foods. I gave it up to the fact that I was doing something wrong.  Well what I learned was Weber has perfected grilling performance and every little detail looks the burners, heat displacement, quality of the grates,  all have something to do with the results of good tasting and appealing food. title: Spirit E-210 Palmetto Roll-out
text:
I bought the E-210 two burner because the two of us rarely grill for more than two and we were replacing a three burner that was really two big. Small can some times not be good because I had a hard time installing a full gas tank as I couldn't maneuver in the small space to reach the tank hanger/gauge. The side wall of the grill is not strong enough to support the full tank so it deflects inside with the weight. This idea of measuring the level of the tank by weight is inaccurate and a waste of time as any one who has a gas grill knows that when fuel runs out it is time to change. And lastly, why is the back of the grill not fully inclosed? How much money can Weber save by eliminating a 24" * 18" piece of sheet metal? I can assure you the local cats and raccoons will soon discover the route to the grease collector and deposit it on the garage floor. 

With that being said, the good points. The grill is overall well made and sturdy. It lights immediately and heats up quickly. The grates are heavy and easy to clean. The grease collection system is well designed and easy to clean. (If you can keep the animals out. I'm having a metal screen made to enclose my grill fully.) Overall I am pleased and satisfied with my purchase.

title: Two q1200 grills fail in same way in a month
text: I am returning a weber q1200 - again. I bought one last fall and it was working great until a few weeks ago. It got used several times a week on our patio. The gas was not getting to the burner to light. I am religious about keeping it clean, making sure the burner holes are clear. One day it just would not light - no gas to the burner. The 5 gallon propane was full. That tank worked on my Nepoleon grill. I bought a new hose, still no gas to the burner. So I bought another Q1200 grill. This one worked for 2 weeks, then again - no gas getting to the burner. Verified it was not the tank or hose. I bought a gas sniffer detector just to verify if any gas was getting through. I saw on line about what to do to "reset" the regulator attached to the grill. Still no gas got to the burner. Also online saw that these grills having the regulator built in the grill fail alot of times. The only was the grill would work was when I attach the small propane cylinder to the grill. Not acceptable to only work with a small cylinder and not the refillable  (or tank exchange) method. So I am getting another Nepoleon travelpro 285 grill. I cannot trust that the weber q1200 will always work anymore with 5 gallon propane tanks.

title: What a great product!
text:

Even though I previously had a Spirit II two burner, I learned how to properly start up the unit.  The instructions had me slowly open the propane gas tank valve and wait a bit to insure gas lines came upto proper pressure.  Then I cranked up the three burners until the temperature rose to 500.  Then I reduced heat to the cooking temperature.  


I have cooked salmon, chicken and flank steak and all were evenly cooked and the temperature held steady.


What a great product!

text:

I'm not disappointed with the choice as it compares well to my old Genesis Silver B which I finally had to retire.  Assembly was relatively easy thanks to the included instructions and the available companion video app which further illustrated each assembly step.  If I have any fault with this grill it would be the wheels which are fairly cheap plastic wheels and actually fell off the grill the first time I had to move it.  I was able to put them back on and they've stayed ever since.

All in all, this is a high performing grill with a plenty of features that I'm still getting used to including the Crossfire ignition system.  The grill heats up plenty fast and clean up has been relatively easy.  The metal is a bit thinner than the Silver B but seems to retain heat (in July) well, even when turned to Low.  I'm quite satisfied with my purchase and would do it again.

title: Disappointment
text: I have owned a number of Weber Grills over the years, starting with a charcoal kettle grill. One of the things that I have been most impressed with all of my grills is the rigid steel construction and heavier weight of the overall grill and carts. This particular grill has been quite the opposite. I really do not care for the cheaply made cart and light weight feel of the lid and grill box. This grill, so far, has been a disappointment. I bought it at one of the "Big Box" stores and paid extra for assembly. The personnel at the warehouse must have been in a hurry and left off both of the metal back covers. This makes the cart flimsy and feel like a number of the lesser priced "knockoff" grills. I immediately reported the issue to Weber (4-6 weeks ago) and was assured that I would be getting both of the missing parts within 7-11 days. So far I have only received the smaller of the two parts. A follow-up by me 7-10 days ago was met with a reassurance that I would be getting the missing part and I just needed to be "patient." Well so far no panel and my patience is all by evaporated. It's truly sad that yet another "benchmark" company has elected to make their products below standards and no longer a cut above the competition.

title: First new BBQ grill in 35 years
text:
After researching  a lot, I chose this E-210 LP gas  grill , 1st because of Weber's warranty and reputation. 2ndly because it had fold down shelves. I've got a smaller deck and wanted a smaller footprint. The size is still big enough for a decent amount of grilling space. It's easy to fold the side shelves up or down and with a good cover and with shelves folded it tucks away nicely in the corner. It ignites immediately, heats up fast and seems to grill evenly. For the limited time used it did a great job on burgers and steaks. Longer usage on different foods is to be determined.  I had it assembled and delivered, with old grill hauled away for free so no hassles there.
The one glaring problem is there is only a short back panel on the back leaving a large opening. This allows wind to blow in, looks unfinished, and because we get critters, they probably will crawl into the grill. My dealer is ordering a second panel to install which should mostly eliminate that problem. It's a strange cost cutting decision because Weber's other grills have a full back panel.
All in all, for the cost and performance this is a great smaller grill choice and recommended. We'll see if it lasts as long as my old 35 year old grill.

title: Just Keeps Getting Better
text:
Since 2002 I’ve had the pleasure of grilling on Weber grills.  This is my third Spirit E-210 Gas Grill.
I appreciate Weber’s innovation over the years - and their commitment to quality components. I’m a “heavy user,” in that I use the grill four or five nights a week. It’s not usual for me to shovel a path through the snow to the grill in the winter. I have to confess my observations and experiences with Weber are overwhelmingly positive.  The rare issues I’ve had with my Weber grills have been external to the product.  The time when squirrels chewed on the rubber gas line, corrosive ocean-salt air, losing a part when moving from one house to another . . .All resolved with help from Weber’s excellent Customer Care representatives.  One last data point to consider when deciding a brand of grill: Weber’s Warranty.  In all my years of using my Weber grills I had an issue with a flavor bar.  The grill was still under warranty and the Customer Care representative sent a replacement. Easy.
In my opinion, Weber honors the values of integrity, quality and customer satisfaction.

title: Hot handle

title: Mixed review:  Good, Bad, and Ugly
text:
Good:  The grill itself is great with flop down shelves and sleek overall design.  Burner knobs and lighter respond quickly.  
Bad:  The wheel locks are hard to access with your foot.  
Ugly:  This issue is not about any visual presentation of the unit.  It is the placement of the propane tank in the cabinet.  My big complaint is the installation of the propane tank.  What would be seemingly an easy concept of placing the tank inside the cabinet and securing with a simple restraining system does not exist.  Rather the engineers and designers thought a system of hanging the tank on a weight hook that visually shows how much propane gas is left in the tank would be a great idea.  So what is the problem with such a clever idea?  Lifting a full propane tank onto the "hook" is nearly impossible unless you are an avid weight lifter or you can get the assistance of another person who can help you lift the tank from the back open side of the cabinet.  Normally we lift heavy objects with our body (torso) over and above the object.  In the case of placing the tank on the weight hook, the body of the solo lifter is in front of the cabinet with only their arms are inside the cabinet.  This arrangement is extremely difficult to do and bad for the back for one person to accomplish.  What makes it even more challenging is the existence of a large round hole in the floor of the cabinet just under the final placement of the tank.  The hole is large enough that the tank slips right through the hole during the attempt to place the tank on the hook.  So what is the purpose of the hole?  It allows the full tank to hang past the cabinet floor.  This hanging system is the ugly part of this grill when the existence of a tank gauge would be a better system of letting the owner know how much gas is still in the tank.

title: 5⭐️ Product and Service
text:
I’ve had many Weber kettles over the 20 to 30 years. The oldest kettle is a little worst for wear now but still in use.  I’ve replaced handles, legs, wheels, grill grates and have added many accessories over the years. I’ve also had a few gas grills in this time but none were Webers.  On day I had the opportunity to pick up a Spirit E-210 from a friend. The grill was a 2013 model and well used. I got it home, I cleaned the ol girl up and to my surprise it was all original. It was missing a few things and the flavorizer bars had seen better days. I went to amazon to get the new parts, which included grease pan, flavorizer bars, new knobs, Igniter kit, (the old one still had the original battery and was working, but was leaking black tar like goop), and the warming rack. The only other thing that was needed was the propane manifold. This was the only part I could not find on amazon. I went to Weber’s website and found the diagram for this model and got the part numbers for everything I needed to insure proper fit on everything before ordering from Amazon. I located the number to customer service and thought what the heck, I’ll case and see if someone will answer.  Now to be honest I wasn’t expecting anyone to answer except maybe a computer, being that it was Sunday evening. SUNDAY EVENING PEOPLE!! I was excited when an actual person, a human a real live human answered the call. Now this guy, I wish I could remember his name, asked a few questions, found the correct part that I was looking for, collected some information and got the grill registered in my name. Within a few days all the new parts arrived, I I got everything installed. The grill is working great and we love it. This ol girl will be around for many more years.  Disclaimer, I truly believe that one of the main factors behind the grill being in such great overall condition, was the Weber cover that was put on after each cook. I’m still using the original cover as it is in remarkable shape considering it’s age. Did I say it was SUNDAY and someone answered the phone?!?
Big shoutout to the Weber family for building such great products and their commitment to customer service.

text: This is our 8th Weber BBQ grill in over 50 years.  We started out with a Smokey Joe when we were first together and several years later upgraded to the larger kettle BBQ. Some years after that we purchased our first Weber gas grill and have stayed with gas ever since purchasing 4 more BBQ’s including two Q 1000’s for camping in our RV.  We had one Genesis grill for over 9 years when I noticed the burners weren’t burning evenly even after I cleaned them.  I called the company to get a replacement model number and the person asked if I had registered the grill when I bought it.  I told her I didn’t remember so she checked for me and told me I had registered the product and she would have new burners sent out the next day free of charge!  That was the only problem we ever encountered with a Weber grill over the years which is amazing because we live in CA and grill probably an average of 3 days a week year round. Our grills have definitely had heavy usage.  We’ve moved into a smaller home recently so we decided to downsize to the Spirit 3 burner grill.  It takes up less space and with the larger wheels it’s easier to move around the backyard.  I’ve been totally impressed with the design and functionality of the grill. I also appreciate how Weber has maintained their basic design but continues to improve their products over the years.  Another testament to the longevity of the Weber grills is that 6 of our old grills found new homes with friends or family members when we upgraded to the next model.  When I’m ready for a new grill I always look at other BBQ’s to see if there’s anything I like better but after doing the research I always end up with a Weber!

The grill feels sturdy and well-designed, perfectly meeting the needs of my small family. In just a month, I've used it twelve times, and it’s been fantastic for grilling vegetables, steaks, burgers, and brats. 

My only minor concern is that a couple of small screws have fallen out, despite tightening them by hand and using a drill for extra security. Overall, based on my experience so far and my previous Weber grill, which lasted over seven years, I would definitely recommend the Spirit E-210.

title: Very sturdy and well built
text: I purchased this grill because the components on it were heavier, sturdier, and thicker than other cheaper grills I looked at and had observed on the curb in my neighborhood waiting on the trash trucks to pick them up.  These cheaper grills looked almost new on the outside, but on the inside they were rusted out, and the metal and grates was thin and cheap.  The Weber Spirit is also easy to remove the grates and other internal components to clean the grill, other cheaper grills require are harder to clean.

title: Owner
text:
Love the grill.  Assembly instructions were easy to follow.  Hardware kit was short one washer and one screw in hardware pack 'C'.  Contacted Weber and they shipped a complete hardware 'C' pack overnight at no cost.  Very pleased with their Customer Service.

The only negative I would add to my experience is the bottom compartment, rear panel has been recently redesigned and  shortened so it doesn't completely hide the LP tank from a rear view of the grill.  The model shown at Lowe's was apparently the previous version had had the larger back panel.  The Customer Service Rep could only say that the larger panel had been discontinued and was no longer available.  No explanation for this change was offered; but I suspect making a larger opening for the tank compartment was for safety.  If the tank leaked, the gas would be able to vent out much easier.  It doesn't look as nice but if the change was for safety, I fully support it.

title: Good Old Grill, But...
text:
Let me preface my review by stating that, over the years, I have owned at least five Weber grills that I can recall. All have lived long, useful lives. All have been easy to operate, until my latest purchase. In April 2024, I purchased a new Weber grill. Overall, it is as easy to use as all my others, except for two things. There is a small ( and I mean small ) hook on the inside of the lid to be used to hang the lid on the side of the kettle. It is so small that a gust of wind caused the lid to fall off, chipping the paint and resulting with my having to deal with customer service. Can you make that hook a little longer?
   Secondly, whoever designed that new ash catcher should be reassigned. Either I am doing something wrong when I try to lower it to dump the ashes or you must have the strength of Arnold Schwarzenegger to get it to work. The old ashcatchers were sometimes tricky to use, but, overall, were MUCH simpler. I am an old guy and my strength, as they say, ain't what it used to be. Also,being an old guy, I remember an expression " if it ain't broke,don't fix it". Now you know why I gave my new Weber grill four stars, not five,

title: Nice Grill - See Suggestions...
text: Weber makes an excellent gas grill. I replaced my 16 year old Weber Genesis with this new Spirit II E-310 Weber grill and it's great. However, I have two suggestions for the Weber design team regarding the E-310: The drip pan is too small and awkward to empty without spillage. Needs improvement. After only two weeks of usage, I had a squirrel gnaw through the gas hose in multiple spots resulting in a LP leak during use! I did not notice damage until it was apparent the burners were not getting as hot as usual. Could have been a problem but shut down safely and replaced with Weber part. Also purchased a cover to help deter the pests. I'd like to see a braided hose for durability. Low cost for added safety.

title: What I wish they would change.
text: It’s ok.  Would prefer the left table have the option to be fixed permanent in the up position instead of just swing down.  Don’t like the way you have to manually light the grill.  Would prefer a hole by the far left burner tube so it can be lighted with a lighter that has a 6 inch extension.  When reaching for items on the back of the grill, you have to use gloves or you burn your skin.  Would prefer the bun warmer swing up when the grill is opened so it’s easier to access the items in the back part of the grill.  Electric start is fine, but would prefer the option to install one of those ignition spark makes (when you push down on the button and it creates a spark).  To obtain a temp around 300 - 500˚ F I use only the outside burners (or any two burners), the center burner is turned off.  My son who is not mechanically inclined was able to assemble the grill by reading the instruction.  There were a few steps that seemed out of place around the wiring section, but he managed to assemble the grill.  Recommend removing the battery in the electric starter after use to prevent battery corrosion.  Other than what I mentioned, it’s ok.

text: Incredibly easy set up, well designed charcoal disposal system and seemingly built to last! I had one of these years ago and regretted giving it away when I moved. I got this grill at Ace and really like the indigo blue color: subtle but unique.

title: I’m not mad, just disappointed
text: My old Weber was approximately 20 years old, had a sturdy frame with square stock and had a removable bottom fire box/pan, never rusted, minimal flare ups, bulky tires, basically heavy duty everything. I didn’t realize until I received my grill that the quality has gone down over the years dramatically. Spending over $500, I expected a lot better. I noticed right away the frame was built cheaper, tires very narrow, could not remove bottom box/pan to clean easily, already have some rust spots after a few weeks with a Weber grill cover, already starting to flare up some. The good news is it does still cook very well. I’m mostly concerned about the longevity of the grill, we cook on it much more than most people and it gets moved a lot as well.

title: TOO BAD FOR US
text:
My first Weber grill (Spirit E-310) was purchased in June, 2016.  It was well used approximately 3 times a week for the past 8 years.  I had to replace the flavor bars a couple of times and finally bought stainless steel cooking grates. The grill was easy to clean with a slide-out bottom tray. I would have kept the grill but the burners started to fail.

I bought a new grill (Spirit II E-310) in September, 2024.  Unfortunately, it's a poor replacement.
Cleaning is a real chore with having to remove the cooking grates and flavor bars exposing the delicate burners to potential damage.  Too bad the sides and doors were removed on the current model since it allows easy access to the catch pan for squirrels and other small creatures.
I've used it about 8 times and cleaned it at least 3 times. Yes, I have a cover, also poorly seamed together.

Too bad for us that I didn't want to spend double the price for the better looking, more quality built model.  I'm surprised Webster has its name on such a low-end product.

Weber sent me replacement "tents" and a new side shelf even though the shelf was damaged by a falling tree. The "tents were available in Lowes for $65 and the shelf would have cost $85. Weber saved me $150 and didn't even ask me to pay for shipping. I will ALWAYS buy a Weber grill going forward!! Thanx!

title: Basic grill, nothing special
text: It's a basic grill that takes longer to cook on then my previous grill that had infrared technology in it. Can't get that good char on my steaks like my previous steaks. Not mad, I would buy this grill again, because the food that I have cooked comes out more evenly cooked then on my past grill. It's easier to clean and keep clean. Glad I built this grill versus letting some kid at the big box store pre assembled it. Hopefully this is the last grill I will have to buy for a while.

title: Perfect size for two!
text: This grill is smaller than our old one, and it is a perfect size for two! Love the built in temperature gauge and the ease of starting it.  This grill heats up quickly and cooks evenly. I’m very pleased with our Weber.

title: Spirit II E-210 Gas Grill
text: This model is much nicer than the original. I like the fact that the propane tank hangs on the side and is much more accessible, and the large wheels make it much easier to navigate.  The open style with shelf is cleaner and does not promote the dampness and clutter of the enclosed compartment of the original model.  Spirit II is a great little grill, we love it.

title: “Best Reliable Grill”
text: Purchased this grill per America’s Test Kitchen’s recommendation. We’ve had it for more than 6 years and it’s great. This replaced another Weber grill that we had for more than 10 years. I do a lot of meal prepping on weekends so I grill several pounds of marinated meats for several days consumption and this grill makes it possible. I recently purchased the griddle insert and love it. Recently, I needed to change the igniter and flavorizer bars, contacted Weber and received the best customer service. Weber ended up sending me the igniter and flavorizer bars for free. Thank you Weber. I highly recommend this grill.

text: We bought a Spirit II 310 in 2009 and it served us well.  The propane jets needed to be replaced along with the flavor bars. So we bought the same model in 2024 and are looking forward to a similar lifespan.  Over the years the grill has improved, 3 burners instead of 2, and hanging the propane tank is the most accurate way of determining how much fuel is left.

title: Great grill, but cumbersome
text:

title: Some people would call these design flaws
text: I mostly like the product except for 2 design flaws in my opinion.  There is no backside panel on it.  The wind can really blow thru it.  It kept blowing the grease pan out of it.  Also you have to hang the propane tank.  That is good if you the grill to keep track on how much propane you have left, but I find it hard to hang due to the weight of a full tank and you have to do it because there is no other place to put it.

title: Love this little grill
text: Perfect size for my husband and I. It’s also heavy duty. We have terrible wind in our area but in the few months we’ve had it the wind hasn’t moved it or blown it over.

title: good 2 burner grill
text:
