The burners work fine, but like the flavor bars, they get soaked in grease as well.  The propane tank attachment is okay, along with the hose and connector.     Other than the cleaning part, I would give it an " A grade"

title: grill time!

title: Quality Compact Grill
text: This is a quality unit that is relatively compact, so it uses less space on a patio or in a garage. I have enjoyed cooking many proteins on it, from burgers and steaks, to fish, chicken, kabobs, etc.

title: Returned to charcoal after 25 years
text: I have not charcoal grilled in maybe 25 years.  My friend and neighbor Tim is a Weber charcoal advocate and I finally became jealous enough to start doing it myself.  Holy cow has Weber gotten even better over time. The ash collector underneath is nothing short of amazing. The porcelain coating makes me think this will last forever. The grates are a breeze to clean. Read the tips and follow them on the website. The lid holder and handles for hanging the grill are an amazing engineering delight.  I think my pellet and NG grill are going to lonely for the next few years.

title: Update to previous review
text: I originally submitted a review that was very critical of my new Weber Spirit E-210 grill.  Prior to this purchase, I had used Weber Q's for 20+ years, upgrading every time I purchased a new one.  When I made this purchase, I was also looking at the Weber Q - 2 burner grill, but decided that I would instead go with the Spirit.  The Weber Q is pretty straightforward to use.  The burners are closer to the grates and I could get a sear and stick to the recommended cooking times.  This grill is a little more intricate, has more parts and requires a little more self-education to figure out how to get a good product.  I am getting there - in part thanks to Weber's excellent customer service.  Following my negative review, a representative reached out to me and has continued to answer questions and be in touch.  With this person's help, my grilling experience has greatly improved.  I give four stars because I am still learning how to use the grill.  But, I definitely give Weber five stars for reaching out to me and actually showing concern about my experience.  And, I expect I'll think this grill was a five star purchase when "The Griller" figures everything out.

title: It’s just right!
text: This is my first time owning a two burner Weber and I am pleased.  It is still a powerful grill the cleans up nicely.  I love it!

title: Hard to beat a Weber

title: Compact, rigid, good design

title: Great once I got used to it

title: Another great grill by Weber
text: Great mid size propane grill.  This is our second Weber propane grill, and 3rd Weber purchased.  Always a great product!

title: Exactly what I needed
text: Keeps the heat, even on our windy deck.  I put a roast on the rotisserie, halfway through, I tossed vegetables into the aluminum tray I had placed below the roast.  Even the 40 degree temperature I was concerned may lengthen the cooking time had no affect on when it was done. On top of that, when I looked to see how much gas was left (we love this added feature by the way) I was amazed that it hardly moved the gage.    Would I buy this again? Absolutely!

title: Very Disappointed in the Spirit E-210 Gas Grill
text: If I had known what I know now when I purchased this grill, I would not have purchased it. I would have purchased another one like my previous grill. With my Tru-Infrared grill, you just placed the propane tank into its circular home in the base of the grill. It's very easy. With this Weber grill, you have to struggle in tight quarters with a heavy propane tank to get the tank onto a hook where the propane level gauge is located. The grease tray attached to the left side of the grill is in the way too. It's too easy to bump your hand against it while struggling to put the propane tank onto the hook. Weber also has a half-panel on the back side of the grill which limits access to putting the propane tank onto the hook from that side. There is no such limiting panel on the back side of my previous grill. I consider the propane level gauge to be rather useless anyway. From what I have read, the accuracy of the gauge is somewhat suspect. I prefer to empty the propane tank, and when it runs out, just switch it out for a second propane tank that I always have on hand. This grill also does not cook the hamburgers as well as my previous grill. I wouldn't have purchased this Weber grill if I had known about all of its shortcomings. Don’t make the same mistake I did.

title: It’s Okay

On my second use I noticed how thin the paint/ enamel coating is when I started seeing scratches through the holes of the top air adjustment. I’m not sure if there is any difference in the quality of the hardware or paint in the Weber master touch series, but the plastic tab on the top air handler would be a nice to have.

I purchased a new weber because I had my old one for 25 years. When I moved, I treated myself to a new grill. However, the new grill is rusting which has never happened to me before with a Weber. They clearly are not the same quality and not worth the price. I should have kept my old  one.

All in all the lesson learned is NOT to get cheap with the grill and trying to save some money. For those looking to get their first ever Weber, I highly suggest getting one with the pan as the ash catcher and a thermometer. Remember: if you're lookin' you aint cookin'

title: Weber made it right!
text:
I initially bought a Spirit II grill and was very disappointed with it's ability to heat above 450F, went threw multiple iterations of remote trouble shooting unsuccessfully, replace the regulator, etc, etc. still no improvements.

So I inquired as to what could be done to return the current unit and replace it with a Genesis, like what we have had for 10+ years at our primary residence and were informed that is not possible.  After finally getting to the right level of support, we proposition was made to purchase a new Genesis for the highly discounted price of $500, MSRP ~$800, and complimentary cover and a free accessory.  We took Weber up on the offer and also took advantage of their flat fee $99 assembly service via Angi.  Everything went as planned, the grill was promptly shipped, the assembler showed up on time and did a great job (we got stuck with have to bring all the packaging to the dump) and we now have a new Genesis, with a Cover and Griddle and managed to sell the original unit of FB Marketplace for $250 - all in all a GREAT OUTCOME and EXCELLENT Customer Service - WELL DONE WEBER!

title: Good Grill, But Make Them Great Again
text: My last Weber Spirit (same size) lasted 13 years so I wanted another one. This one performs fine, no complaints on actually grilling on it so far. However, during assembly I noticed a pretty significant drop in overall quality compared to my last one. The grill has an open back rather than fully enclosed. Everything feels cheaper on it, the steel, burners, drip bars, handles, etc.... I am hoping it's all just cosmetic, but I will be surprised to get anywhere near the lifespan out of this one. Other than that I feel like it still is the best option within that price range. I also have had good experiences replacing worn parts with Weber's so that's reassuring. I wish weber would make these in the USA with a little better attention to quality.

The best design would be to be able to carry the tank to the bracket while in a standing position, enabling the user to use the bigger and stronger leg and upper back muscles to load the tank onto the hook. title: Three-burner Marvel
text:
This is our first Weber Grill. We have several friends who have them and without exception they rave about their grill’s high quality construction and performance. When our grill was ready for grill cemetery, we decided we wanted a Weber Grill.

One of the “must have” features for us was fold down sides. Because of where our grill is used and stored between uses, we wanted this feature. We also determined that a three-burner grill would best meet our needs both for cooking area, physical size and great grilling performance. With this in mind we searched on line and found that perfect Weber three-burner grill minus the fold-down sides. 

Nonetheless, we decided to go to Lowe’s and check out all grills in person. When we described our wish list to the salesman, we were thrilled that the new line of Weber Grills now included a three-burner model with fold down sides. After lifting the cover and turning the dials, the quality construction of the Weber Grill was obvious and we made the purchase.

After using the grill several times, we could not be happier with our decision. It cooks very evenly and offers great control over temperature. Preheating is fast and the searing feature is a bonus. 

If there is any learning curve, it would involve the lighting process.  You must read the manual to properly ignite the burners. On most grills, it is rather intuitive.  Not so on the Weber.  Pushing in on the knob, holding it in for 2 seconds, turning to the ignite position while continuing to push in and then continuing to push inward for an additional 2-5 seconds until the burner ignites.  Once mastered, not an issue.  But if a guest at your cookout offers to start your grill, tell them thanks but you’ll do it. 

I give this grill a 5-star rating without hesitation and highly recommend it. Quality and performance are excellent. I have never looked forward more to grilling, than I do now with this Weber Grill.

title: Well built, but lacks in radiant heat.
text:
The grill quality is excellent and what I expected from Weber and the price point. The assembly was easy for one person to build. There is a lot of packaging making sure nothing is bend or broken. The burners and lighters are very well build. Flareups are uncommon due to the design of the burners and burner shields. Heat distribution is very even across the grill. 

I would prefer that there was a rear wall to the grill base.

The grill is smaller than I am used to, but it is perfect for my family of (3) and can easily cook for a small crowd. 

The grill grates are fine, but they need to be heavier to create better grill marks. There is also a large gap in between the two grates that might loose hot dogs or asparagus while grilling. 

The heat retention is the only real setback for this grill. I purchased in cooler months (60*F ambient) and although the grill easily reaches 500*F when heating up, the heat is all lost as soon as the lid is open. The stainless burner shields are thick and the burners themselves are well designed, but even with the sear setting on, the radiant heat needed to sear and create grill marks just isn’t there. Burgers and salmon look more baked than grilled at times. 

I think during hot 100*F summer days that the heat retention will not be a problem, but I do like to grill year round. 

I am very glad I didn’t save a few dollars buying the two-burner version of this grill.

title: Poor Quality Undercarriage
text:
The Weber Original Kettle Premium 22" Charcoal Grill cooks well but is let down by a flimsy undercarriage. The kettle excels: it spreads heat evenly, with adjustable vents for precise temperature control (250°F-500°F). The porcelain-enameled grates are durable, and the One-Touch ash catcher makes cleanup simple.

However, the legs and wheels—thin aluminum and plastic—are too weak. Moving the grill requires caution; uneven surfaces or grass can jam the wheels, bending or collapsing the legs. The undercarriage’s poor quality doesn’t match the sturdy kettle, and the legs will likely fail first.

For the price tag, the grill’s legs should use thicker aluminum or steel for stability.  The kettle’s great, but the weak frame means I won’t buy again.

Handle it delicately—it’s fragile!

text:
Unfortunately, my experience with this Weber grill has been highly disappointing. The materials used feel cheaper than expected, and the lid and grill box arrived defective/damaged. Every time the lid is opened or closed, it produces an irritating clunking noise that is already causing ware to the outside edge of the grill box.
Adding to the frustration, working with Weber Customer Service has been a challenging ordeal. Initially, I spoke with an agent who assured me she would resolve the issue but then transferred my claim to another department that “only communicates via email”.
2 days after talking to the first agent, I got an email from the “Spirit Team Specialist” requesting my shipping address (Despite providing my shipping address through warranty registration). In his email states “apologize for the damage - I’d be glad to assist you - please confirm your shipping address – we hope your issue has been resolved; though I had no clarity on what had been resolved or what was being shipped.
Attempts to follow up by phone resulted in more runaround with another agent explaining that the matter was being handled by a specialist who could only be reached via email—a method that promised no response for 24-48 hours. Eventually, the “Spirit Team Specialist” called to offer a free accessory for the inconvenience and promised to send a new grill box and lid while attempting to find someone to replace the damaged parts. However, they warned that scheduling this technician might take 24-48 hours, followed by an additional 4-5 business days for them to arrive.
When I expressed dissatisfaction with this offer, the specialist consulted with his manager and proposed shipping a brand-new grill. However, this option required self-assembly as Weber would not honor assembly by Ace Hardware (which had assembled the original grill). When I declined this, the specialist said they would “get back to me,” but I’m still waiting after more than 24 hours.
At this point, I regret my purchase and wish I had opted for a less expensive $100 throw a way grill!

The design is timeless—sleek, sturdy, and compact enough for a small patio, yet spacious enough to grill for a group. The 22-inch cooking surface gives me plenty of room to handle everything from burgers and hot dogs to ribs and whole chickens.

What really stands out is how well it retains and distributes heat. The adjustable vents make temperature control a breeze, whether I’m going low and slow or searing steaks over high heat. The ash catcher system is also a game-changer—it makes cleanup fast and easy, which is a big plus.

Overall, the Original Kettle is a must-have for charcoal grill lovers. It’s affordable, durable, and delivers that unbeatable smoky flavor every time. Whether you're a grilling newbie or a seasoned BBQ pro, this grill is a fantastic choice!

Power: However, considering power and area, the E-325 appears to be the better option, as it achieves 86 BTU/sq in (according to Weber's website), while the E-425 is slightly lower at 82 BTU/sq in. I don't think this one will last 3 yrs IF lucky! Had problems the entire first 2 weeks we bought it. Due to Weber Customer Service did not really understand what was going on was supposed to be normal come to find out. Very just disappointed. The grease pan needs replaced every week as it is so much smaller. Do NOT like the Open Cabinet at all when living in the Country especially. Every Animal finds a new home in it. That Flavorizer Bar in the back is useless except for something that will need replacing all the time. The actual 3 Flavorizer Bars for the grill are made THIN like the 1 and 2 hundred dollars no name brand grills. The way the grease catcher in the bottom is made, you constantly have to drag it out to clean it. From the back. And seems like a fire hazard the entire way it is designed. We don't use the sear thing. Kinda useless for us. And no way to grill over 3 steaks especially if large ones so forget about company. If just 2 people and not grilling an entire family pack of pork chops or chicken for left overs forget about it unless you want to grill 2 sets of meat. Those sides that left up & down are not stable enough to be constantly moving. Waiting on those to snap. And don't understand why the top is not full metal but some type of plastic. IF you plan on using it once in a while and not daily. Plus only 2 people it MIGHT be okay. We would have came out better rebuilding the old Spirit Propane Grill. And forget about lighting it with new setup they have. Each burner has its OWN lighting system. And IF you have wild animals every where, they are going to chew that up first.

I only found out after purchasing that this $250 grill does not come with a simple heat resistant plastic handle for the dome damper that weber probably makes for a few pennies, and includes on higher end models… I consider that a miss on webers part, not including this could also be considered a safety flaw. Think about it. Its a part that is meant to be handled many times while cooking, and could easily cause burn injuries without using appropriate precautions.
Weber needs to step up and provide this part on all of their grills.
In the past i had bought a small $15 throwaway kettle for a temporary work site that had a heat resistant damper handle, but weber doesn’t provide one on the premium kettle?
I found a few aftermarket pieces that will fit, but most are out of stock. Now I know why.

title: Can Weber Right the Ship??
text: I bought this model largely on the strength of the brand name, as well as the table-top size.  The results have been mixed, and my rating could just as easily be two stars as three.  It worked well, but the regulator lasted only about 10-12 uses, requiring me to get a new one from Weber.  Fortunately the grill was one month within its warranty period so they sent me one for free, but the Internet is full of bad comments about this exact problem so it is likely one of inherent design and build.  In other words, this is not a reliable grill for long-term service right out of the box.  If I were a Weber executive this fact would frighten me to death.  Because of the early failure of the regular, I no longer have respect for Weber gas grills and will likely look elsewhere for my next model.  That is a real shame.  What griller has not seen or used a Weber kettle somewhere?  I suspect that the grill parts (all or some) are no longer made in the U.S.A. and have used cheap materials and construction to keep costs down.  This will kill Weber in the long run.  I hope this new regulator that I installed will work for a long time.  I wish I had the confidence to say that I think it will.  Sadly, I think my experience is one of many such experiences, and is likely the tip of the iceberg that will sink what I once thought was the best brand out there.

text: Decent grill, terrible grill plates and top rack.  The grill is compact, so users are clearly going for a maximum grilling area versus total space taken up by the grill.  I was shocked to see the grill plates have an enormous gap where they meet in the middle.  All of my prior grills had plates that had a solid metal piece in the middle (i.e., where the plates meet) so that grilling area could be used as well. Not this Weber grill--it has a grand canyon-sized gap where the grill plates meet due to the metal knobs on the ends of the grill plates. I can only assume that this saved a few cents per grill and was an efficiency measure implemented by the Weber C suite folks.  I couldn't be more disappointed for a grill at this pricepoint.  The gap is so large it renders the middle of the grill functionally unusable for many grilling items, such as chicken cutlets, fresh-pattied hamburgers (fall apart through the gap), hot dogs/brats, asparagus/peppers/smaller veg, etc.  What's even more frustrating is that the floor models at my local harware stores and the photos Weber shows online ALL conceal this gap. title: Not as stated on web site
text:
I bought this grill because my wife and I wanted to downsize while still having a grill that would allow us to grill and griddle at the same time. As a result, I needed a model that would allow half of the grill surface to be replaced as needed with a griddle top. Weber's site listed a half griddle as an accessory for this unit, so I bought it plus the griddle. 

Well guess what? The half griddle that was listed as an accessory is for the *old* Spirit E-325 and does not work with this one. This knowledge was gained by actually using the griddle and grill, thereby making both unreturnable. So I am now the  owner of a grill that doesn't have the main feature I wanted, plus a pricey griddle insert that doesn't work for the grill. 

Hey Weber, here's a couple of ideas for you:
1. Don't reuse product names/model numbers over and over. It makes it real **** hard to figure out what works with what. The "new" E-325 has different starter mechanisms, different grill grates and different accessory compatibility. USE A NEW MODEL NUMBER. Reusing the model number is confusing and misleading. 
2 Update your **** web site in a timely fashion. This griddle was listed as a compatible option for several weeks while I decided what I wanted to do. 

Does the grill work? Sure. The problem is that right now it's a $300+ purchase I can neither take back nor use exactly as I intended so every time I look at it, it makes me mad and my opinion of it and Weber as a whole will reflect this situation.

title: Follow up customer service
text: The grill was given to me as a gift with HIGH accolades. It worked well for a number of times prior to July 4th. On this date, when started, after ignition, there was a loud hissing, upon inspection, there was a fire at the regulator underneath. we were able to suppress the fire and inspect the regulator connections with the customary soap and water test. There was a leak at the regulator. A replacement regulator was purchased, installed and tested same as above. There were no more leaks, and the grill has functioned ok since then. I reported the incident. The customer service insisted that the case be directed to the incident review team. It was directed immediately, and I provided all requested pictures. They determined that it was a faulty tank, despite that tank being used prior to and since the incident. I disagree with their assessment.  I am disappointed and absolutely astonished that , at no point, did anyone request that I return the regulator that was removed for inspection.  This is amazing and , I feel, a negligent, irresponsible reply.

title: Poor performance
text:
Extremely disappointed in the overall performance of this grill. I previously owned a Q 1000 for many years, and that grill was fantastic, unfortunately because of some damage I bought the Q 1200 as a replacement. Almost two years of use now, and I find that the performance lacking compared to my old Q 1000. Recently, the grill would not heat up well, barely making 500°, and after adding some steaks the temperature would drop to near 400° which it would never recover from. This of course led to poor searing of the meat, so basically a light brown and warm steak. My previous Q 1000 worked equally as well as my Summit and Genesis at home.

I went through all the troubleshooting steps for low heat and yellow flame. As of now I have replaced the regulator, the hose from the problem tank to regulator, and the burner tube. Additionally, I also tried cooking with the 1lb propane bottle to isolate my large tank from the equation. It now will heat up to 550° and did a great job searing my steak on one side. After turning the steak, the temperature dropped as I opened the lid to quickly flip the steak. At this point I once again noticed the temperature not recovering and now the entire burner tube was all yellow flames. Again, no sear on the second side, and another ruined steak. 
 
I have given up on the Q 1200 and really any Q product at this point. If I could go zero stars I would.

text:
This is my second Webber Spirit grill. I was very pleased with my previous Spirit with the exception of the rusting out of the wheels from the base. I was happy to receive and assemble my replacement Spirit grill. Unfortunately, when I first tried to use it, I found the right control knob difficult to turn. The more I tried to turn it the more difficult it became. It froze in place and stripped the inside of the control knob. I eventually reached Fabiano at Webber and described the problem. He asked if I would try to turn what he referred to as the pin that the control knob fit onto with my fingers. I explained I had tried that to no effect. Eventually he asked me to send him a video of the problem. After several frustrating communications via unsuccessful calls and emails I asked to speak with his supervisor.  Whoever he referred it to, understood the problem and accepted our description, agreed to send out the replacement parts. Dealing with Fabiano was very frustrating. Yesterday we received the replacement parts as promised. I will attempt to replace the damaged parts using the replacement parts. 
Dealing with Fabiano was difficult and upsetting. It was like he did not believe me when I described the problem. It should not have been that difficult or take so long to correct the problem. 
I now look forward to replacing the parts and enjoying the use of my new Spirit grill.

title: Stopped working after using a few times
text:
Wow, what a fantastic 5-year warranty I have on my barbecue... said no one ever. The sticker on the grill says 5 years, but surprise! The gas regulator, which apparently is the part that decides whether my grill works or not, only has a 2-year warranty hidden in the fine print.

When I called for support, the agent kindly offered to sell me a new regulator for $80. Because, you know, I'm made of money. But hey, being the thrifty customer I am, I did some research and found the exact same regulator on Amazon for $30. Score!

So, I asked for a price match, and the agent graciously gave me a 20% discount. I mean, who doesn't love saving $10? But the cherry on top was when she warned me against buying "substandard" regulators from Amazon... the same product that has a 4.8-star rating and has been purchased by over a thousand happy customers.

I think it's safe to say who's selling the substandard product here. Weber, you might want to work on your warranty game and customer service skills. 1 star from me, that's being generous. Sorry, 1.2 stars with 20% extra to make it fair and square.
Cheers!

title: Just perfect, except...
text:

My new E-325 propane grill, although only a few weeks old, is on track to maintain that standard.  It arrived in perfect condition, not assembled and with all the parts, in an indestructible box.  Assembly took me slightly more time than indicated, but was easy enough for a DIYer.  The assembled grill is very sturdy, unlike some of the grills I have seen in stores.  I have used it perhaps 10 times already on a variety of food products (vegetables, poultry, fish, meat) and have been pleased with the results in all cases.  The burner  controls make it easy to maintain an even temperature, the grates are easy to remove and clean, and the fold-down side tables make a small footprint for storage.  

There is one drawback for me.  There are only two wheels included; one end of the grill must be lifted in order to move the grill.  This may be more of an issue for me since I store the grill after every use.  If only Weber would send me another complete wheel assembly for the other end, I would be extremely happy with my conversion for charcoal to propane!!!

text:
When paying a premium price for a grill, I expected a much better build quality than what is apparent with my E325. The small plastic wheels don’t roll easily (especially on rough surfaces or grass), and the axle they are mounted on noticeably bends and flexes under the weight they’re trying to support. I expected this unit to be much easier to roll around than my previous (cheaper) grill, but alas, it is more difficult. The grill itself works well enough, but it’s hard to tell if the burner has been lit when you initially start it. You can’t see the flame. I put my hand over it to feel the heat if/when it lights. 
I do like how the heat is well distributed, fairly even across the whole grill surface. 
I wish there was some kind of screen across the back to keep mice and squirrels out, or an enclosure on the back of the control box. The wires on my last grill were chewed up by squirrels; I’m afraid of that happening again with my new, much more expensive grill.

title: Nice Grill
text:
Grilling with the E-325 propane grill is quick, easy, and convenient. Charcoal grills have their place, but in our case, since we have a covered lanai and have to move the charcoal grill from the lanai to the yard whenever we use it (so we don't smoke ourselves out), we decided to add a propane grill to our cooking arsenal.

The E-325 fits our needs perfectly. It's a good size both for transport in the back of our car from the local Lowe's warehouse and for daily use on the lanai.

The three burners get the grill up to temperature quickly and it's very easy to maintain a precise temperature with the control knobs. Usability is great. While casters on the two feet that don't have wheels would have made the grill easier to move around, the overall design is still user-friendly. The one-handed burner lighting and the integrated work surfaces - with their hammered steel look and built-in tool hangers - are pretty nice features. The burners seem well-protected so maintenance should be easy.  We've used this just a few times now, and each time the grill has worked great without any problems or issues.

Aesthetically, I really prefer the black enamel look for where we have this grill located. It's low-key and utilitarian versus shiny and excessive. We've always had stainless steel grills at our primary residence, and while stainless can look good (especially when new) it's sort of a pain to keep it looking good. A cleaning product like "Bar Keepers Friend"  is essential for stainless steel maintenance. All you'll need is a soapy wet sponge for cleaning the exterior of the Weber E-325.

This grill has been enjoyable to use and has produced good results. We can't ask for much more.

title: E325 replaced E320
text: The new E325 replaced my old E320 after 11 years of service. Given we live near the Atlantic ocean, the old unit held up pretty well. The shell was nearly intact (slight rust) but the flavor bars had to be replaced several times, and finally the gas manifolds and connecting tubes all fell apart. Both are 3 burner models. The new one was less money than to old one (no side burner that never got used), but the construction is a lot flimsier - thin walls, door, cheap wheels and axles, only 2 wheels not 4, no wheel locks, grill is a casting not SS rods. So given inflation, the new unit was far less expensive than the original. The E325 has high-temp setting on the center & right burners for searing (old one didn't), and it seems to preheat faster. Cooking is about the same, and produces excellent cooked foods. The side tables fold down, a nice feature. I bought a pressure gauge to check the propane level; it works but is very hard to read since the tank is under the grill. It takes a small mirror to see the gauge dial. The burners blew out once because of a breeze. Perhaps I will need to block off one side of the grill's air-holes because I grill year-round. The ACE people were excellent in delivery and placing it on our deck.

text: This grill went together easily, and while I would have liked the classic black, I got an excellent deal from in a sort of Lowes blue. I like the coal baskets that Weber offers - allowing me to separate or concentrate the heat. And I've used classic charcoal, lump charcoal (and a combination). I've used soaked wood chips as well as soaked wood chunks, too.  I've made ribs, pork, chicken, burgers, steaks (think as well as thin), chops, whole fish, a whole turkey, sausage (and peppers) and more. Tried the snake method for a longer and slower cooks, using some hardwood for smoke. I love the design of this grill - and its size.  The lid hook is nice to use, but I did also get the add on lid holder - and tend to use that more.  I added the Weber tool hook accessory which fits nicely and lets me keep the cleaning tools handy.  I even spring for the rotisserie feature which not only lets me do the spinning cook, but also offers the increased cooking chamber height by adding the ring. Big turkey fits happily in that space. I like the top and bottom vents - which help with air flow control.  The ash cleanup system is a very nice innovation. I keep this grill out of the garage year-round, but always under a Weber cover. It looks nearly new. I picked up a curved plastic scraper for when I want to do more deep cleaning of the bowl. Surprised I have not seen the Weber version of this tool offered.  The kettle is a nice complement to my Weber fleet of grills (which now includes a pellet smoker). Admittedly, I am a Weber fanboy.

title: My 3rd Weber grill in 10 years
text: I stepped into my Local ACE Hardware store here in Texas and the store manager said hey did you know we were having a Labor Day sale on our Grills?  I said no I just need trimmer line. He then began the pitch, after about 10 minutes he had me over in the grill display area and I was kind of impressed with the prices I must admit. This was definitely a real deal for these grills, he had 3-4 different brands. Of course I was and am partial to Weber. He asked me a few very pertinent questions and said check em out I'll be right back. In about 5 minutes I had looked at most everything and had come to the conclusion it would be a good thing with these prices to really consider a new one. When the manager returned he handed me a flyer that had 10%off on any grill in the store. It was a national coupon so it wasn't the main discount, it was on top of what the store had already marked off. I did a couple of calculations and then it hit me, I wonder what the online website has these priced at?  So without him watching I pulled up the Weber site and amazingly enough one of the models that was right in front of me was on sale as well on the website and it was better than his price. I told him what I had found, and he said hang on let me see if we price match. He came back and said we will match that price but we can't do the coupon, I said well how about my military discount I always get, he said well that's a different story. Let me go make a call. In a couple of minutes he was back and said we really have to honor the military at 10% off as well, I got my Spirit E-210 Weber Grill for 195.00 off and they delivered it. I told 5-6 people of this super fantastic offer and 2 of them bought that weekend. My old grill was donated and life is good. I really wanted a new Genisis but I was happy with the one I managed to secure at that great price. The Genisis will have to wait for a little while longer. Weber grills are tried and true I sold them at Sears back in the day. Sold more Weber than any other grill even more than the Craftsmans.  I highly recommend the new models.  Weber has made so many nice upgrades and they stand behind their products.

title: What happened
text:
I’ve been eying this green version for years and I finally pulled the plug and got one. I grew up using Webers only ever owning Weber kettles. Never wanted to look at anything else cooks great food easy to use easy to assemble reliable durable until this one. The metal felt a little thinner the tolerances weren’t as snug but I let that go thinking I might be over thinking it, but after my first cook I noticed the the side handle was bending up and the enamel was chipping away at the seems. 


To put this in perspective I live in an 100 year old wooden house so I have to roll the grill through the yard to a safe distance to cook nothing difficult nothing I would expect any other Weber I’ve had to have problems with.

I did reach out to Weber and the team kindly sent me another kettle bowl to replace mine and it was a very good experience with customer service so I do appreciate that. I was dismayed though when I wheeled the grill out a bit to work on installing the new bowl the handle bent more and the lid went tumbling and got scuffed up. Which is a painful experience to someone like me who likes to keep the grill immaculate.


Over the years I learned to grill on a red 1970s kettle that lasted until 2010 the I had an 18 kettle and upgraded finally to this my dream grill I wish i could have afforded the performer though because at least I would still have a grill in good condition 


Weber please do better it’s what you are capable of that made this so disappointing.

title: Great design
text: I am very happy with my purchase. This BBQ addresses all of the design flaws of previous BBQs I have owned. It is easy to fully clean, with a removable bottom assembly and easy access fat tray. Debris will not build up and interfere with the burners. The burners are solid tubes with no compression points, the usual spot for burners to rust out. The unit heats quickly and holds heat well. The grills are solid cast metal that are widely spaced and easy to clean. The side shelves are solild ceramic covered metal, eliminating the grease stain issue with plastic shelves. The handle is solild metal, including the brackets that mount to the lid which will ensure they will last compared to other BBQs. This is a quality product that fully justififies its higher price.

title: Safe Gourmet Grilling
text:
An outstanding grill! Some major improvements over the earlier Weber grill that I owned for over ten years!

Use anthracite lump charcoal, an electric element starter, mesquite wood chips (soaked in water then drained), and a drip pan centered on the lower grate. 

Slow cook regulating airflow (aka ‘mass flow rate’ 🌟) through the grill, and adding mesquite when 70% cooked. Prepare for a delicious meal—beef, poultry, fish, and smoked vegetables.

Grilling Tip: remove the dome as INFREQUENTLY as possible. Gourmet grilling is an art that requires patience and love for your family and guests. We advise not rushing the creative process. Simplify, Simplify, Simplify. 

No potentially dangerous gas tanks, no lugging empty gas cylinders, no traveling with full gas cylinders (probably without in-vehicle safety restraints) in your personal vehicle, no use of toxic liquid fire starting fluids.

When you are finished grilling, simply close the top and bottom air vents. Anthracite irregular-sized hard lump coal now starved of oxygen goes out reliably and safely.

text: I purchased my Weber E-325 thru Costco and had it shipped to my home.  This grill is replacing an 18-year-old Genesis 300 series grill that is worn out due to the grill case having a hole that burnt thru after many years of use.  It still cooks wonderful but has become dangerous to light.  My wife and I decided we needed something smaller for the 2 of us.  The Weber Spirit series had everything we needed.  The package arrived on a Friday and when I got home from work and began to unbox and assemble it.  The box was completely undamaged, no hole, rips visible.  As I removed the pieces and I found the side, bottom and door were bent, the side was extremely bend.  I'm guessing that it bounced around in shipping and cause the damage.  I was sad and upset but went ahead a registered the grill.  I sent a warranty complaint / claim at the same time.  Saturday morning, I decided to call Weber and verify my claim.  I spoke to a real person who was very helpful.  She did find my claim and apologized for the inconvenience.  She said she would resolved my issues and asked for pictures of the damaged parts.  She sent me a link via text while on the phone with her to upload the pictures.  Easy as pie!  She reviewed the pictures while I was on the phone with her and confirmed that replacement parts are being sent to my home.  I received my parts 4 days later and finished assembling my grill.  The grill lights easy, cooks great like my old weber.  Very pleased with Weber and their customer service.  I have had other grills over the last 40 years, but nothing beats a Weber!  Make sure to register your model & serial number.   They honor warrant claims for some pieces for years.

title: An Excellent First Kettle Grill That Delivers.
text:
As a first-time kettle grill owner, I did my research and landed on the Weber 22” Master-Touch™ Charcoal Grill in Deep Ocean Blue — and I couldn’t be happier with the decision. Weber’s reputation in the grilling world is well-earned, and this grill backs it up.

Appearance

The Deep Ocean Blue finish is stunning. It stands out from the standard black kettle grills you see everywhere and adds a real personality to your backyard setup. It’s the kind of grill that draws compliments before you even fire it up.

Setup & Ease of Use

Assembly is straightforward and well thought out. Everything fits together cleanly, and the instructions are clear enough that you won’t be scratching your head for long. For a first-time charcoal griller, that confidence boost right out of the box matters.

Temperature Control

The damper vent system gives you solid control over airflow and heat management. There’s a natural learning curve to dialing in your ideal cooking temperature, but the system is logical — adjust the vents, monitor the heat, and fine-tune from there. After a cook or two, it starts to feel very intuitive.

Lid Holder

The built-in lid holder on the bowl is a genuinely useful feature, keeping the lid secure and out of your way while you tend to the fire or manage your food. One word of caution though — sliding the lid in and out of the holder can scratch the paint over time. If keeping that beautiful Deep Ocean Blue finish in perfect condition is important to you, handle it with a little extra care.

Bottom Line

The Weber Master-Touch is a fantastic entry point into charcoal grilling. It’s well-built, easy to get started with, and comes from a brand that has been trusted for decades. Minor paint scuffing aside, this grill checks every box. Highly recommended.

title: Things change, but for the better?  Time will tell
text:
We are long time Weber Grill owners and supporters.  We have owned a Weber Grill of one model or another for the last 40 years.  This new Grill (E325) is pretty good, however there has been noticeable pullback in the quality of materials used in making the product.  The folding side tables are not stainless steel, the lid side castings and metal center are lighter weight materials (not as robust), the wheels are cheap plastic & located on one side of the grill rather than the casters on all four corners and The Rear Of The Compartment (where propane tank is held underneath) Has An Open Back.  The open back allows animals to enter to get to the grease catcher or seek shelter and build nests.  The previous models we owned all had enclosed areas underneath to keep the critters out.
I like the "Sear Zone" and it works pretty well.  The starting & temperature setting procedure is a little "non-intuitive".  I understand it, but if I ask someone else who does not own one of these grills to start and set the temperature it is likely not going to get done properly or at all.  I also miss the propane tank holder that let me know when the tank was getting near empty (Lite).  The Temperature guage is always fogged up inside the glass (my previous grill that lasted 10 years did not do that?)
I guess I will need to wait to see how the grill holds up over time.  I do like the grill and how it cooks the things I need it to. I do still feel the grill appears a "good value" if it holds up over time (versus buying 2 or 3 cheaper grills over the same time period).  I don't like to feed the local landfill with rusted out grill remnants.  
So far, all is good with the new Weber.

text: Had one back in the 90s loved easy to clean and food taste sooo good thanks Weber

title: The best Grills

title: Generally good but...
text: The ignition of the burners is weird. It takes us awhile to get it started. Not a intuitive or smooth as other grills.

title: Durable and transportable
text: Everyone needs a portable grill like this one. The wheels are sturdy enough to maneuver over most terrain. The grill itself is a comfortable weight and size to throw into to your truck for transport. I love how the grill is big enough to grill a meal the entire day, but doesn't take up so much space. We took it out on a lake day and had such a great time with it. Thanks to our Weber, we had warm, fresh food the entire day.

title: Well Built, Cooks Very Well
text: Built very well, cooks great, holds heat and overall very impressed. Substantially better thany last one.

title: Plastic Leg Failed Dinner in the Dirt
text: Was carefully moving grill on wheeled cart when plastic grill front leg failed under its own weight, toppling Memorial dinner on the ground.  Who designs grills with 100% plastic structural legs?  Weber does.  Grill was 18 months old, but not sure I can trust the $80 replacement part either.

title: Spirit E-325 Gas Grill
text: This grill is just what I needed to grill for friends and family.  It was great to see how easily it lit with the three burners having their own ignitor. I would highly recommend this grill.  It is not often you can buy a product with a 10 year warranty.

title: Perfect sear
text: Great temperature control and it gets so hot you can get a perfect sear on your ribeye. It’s the perfect portable gas grill in my opinion!

title: Performance
text: Bought it a month ago and it is the best barbaque I have ever used.Love it

title: From intimidated to loving charcoal grilling
text: This 22” weber kettle grill has easily become my go to grill, I used to be intimidated by charcoal grilling, but honestly, it’s not that complicated. It only takes a little more time to get started and the flavor is far superior to electric grills. The grates have been easy to clean and it lightweight and portable which is a huge plus for me. A couple downsides to me are the ash catcher doesn’t always catch ash or hot coals. Finding the lid hook can be a little tricky at first but I quickly got used to it. The last drawback is lack of prep space. After using several other grills, I realized I took for granted having shelves or areas to set down food, utensils, or thermometers. Overall, this grill performs great, the food taste amazing and I’m happy I had the chance to try and review it.

title: Pretty good grill
text: Hubby does the grilling and while he likes this one, he wishes the grates were a little closer together to prevent small nugget of chicken from falling through!

title: Love it
text: Great product. My last Weber was over ten years old and still worked. I gave it to my granddaughter. Love the quality and ease of use. I also like that the side tables fold down. Not having a striker (ignition) button is great. Would recommed to anyone.

title: Love it
text: I use it more than my gas grill. Definitely a great buy!

title: Weber BBQ’s are the best
text: Love the searing controls and the ability to remove the fire box drip area for cleaning.

title: Great grill of you don’t mind 350 degrees.
text: The grill is a perfect size for 2 people.  My only complaint is it won’t go over 350 degrees.  So I bought a large propane tank since that was a suggestion when they don’t get hot enough and it still isn’t getting up to 400.  I also did the reset in case I did something wrong but that didn’t help either.  So it’s well made just won’t get hot enough and for the initial cost and then added expense it should work seamlessly from the get go.

title: Cheap product, awful customer service.
text: Awful quality and customer service. I purchased a stealth premium kettle from Lowe’s and the grill has had so many quality controls issues. The legs and dampers had chipped paint and grill grate would not sit flat, it would wobble no matter what orientation it was in on the grill. To address the grate issue I was first sent a new grate, that didn’t fix the problem. I was first told the chipped paint didn’t affect performance so they treated that like a non issue until a customer service “specialist “  started to reply to the emails. He got replacement parts sent out for the parts with chipped paint then also told me the prongs that hold the grill grate were misaligned and I was being sent a new bowl as well. The replacement bowl shows up with paint damage so I emailed Weber back about that issue then they ghosted me. Never responded back. I had to find their number on the better business bureau website to escalate the issue. Beware of the awful quality control on their products and their horrible customer that just stops responding. Very unprofessional from someone who was a “specialist” lmao. I will not be purchasing any Weber products in the future. Which is a shame because their summit Kamado looked sweet but no way I’m dropping that kind of money when their quality is very inconsistent and poor customer service to support you when you have issues.

title: OK but
text:
This is my first Natural gas grill so I have nothing but LP grill to compare.  I like the grill it does cook differently than my 17 year old lp grill but that might be suspected.  There are still some hot spots.
Please note that I did not assemble this grill my self and did not see a parts list.
My biggest concern is that it is more difficult to light, the one, facing the grill, left burner.  I will address this soon.  the other concern is that the front legs, or legs without the wheels seem flimsy and offer no protection for the floor and may bend if not moved carefully.  I wish there were wheels with locks on all four wheels.   
It is still a weber and I have used Weber gas grills for 40 years they are great grills with lots options for parts and rebuilds.

title: Really great design
text: This military edition is very sharp.  I got the cover so I can keep it as nice as possible for as long as I can.  First two grills confirm the design is terrific to get a fire going, using vents to control temps, and cooking both direct and indirect very well.  I am extremely pleased with this purchase.

title: Best Grill Around for a reason
text: Best All Around Grill for Beginners and the Experienced alike.

title: New to charcoal
text: I always cooked on weber gas grills in the past and aside from the bi-annual grate and flavor bar replacements I loved grilling on them. Recently and after a cross country move I opted for a charcoal kettle grill. So far, no problems with the grill but there is/will be a learning curve. I am not sure if I would attempt to roast a turkey or prime rib roast on the charcoal grill like I did several times a year on my gas grills. Adding fresh charcoal and the nasty smoke smell does not seem like a good idea.

title: Weber E-325 Cooking Grates
text: Cooking grates do not clean off as well as expected

title: The grill I always wanted, and have again
text: Had to give up my first Weber grill due to a move a decade ago. Moved again and got the improved version with the ash catcher and other accessories. Grill love even better second time around.

title: Doesn’t Heat Up Enough

title: Portable
text: We've been enjoying this Weber charcoal grill so far. I love that it's on wheels and it's lightweight so it's easy to move around. It's nice that we can just throw it in the back of the truck and take it with us whenever we need. It's great for picnics and tailgating and we can't wait to take it camping one day. It heat up nice and evenly and so far everything we've eaten from the grill has been yummy!

title: Spirit E325
text: This year I invested in a Weber grill rather than by another three year throw away grill and I am glad I did.  The sale price made it possible.  This is a well constructed, heavy duty grill that does the job.  I have only used it three or four times since purchase, but it is easy to clean, heats evenly, and the drop down side trays make storage much easier.

title: Love this grill

title: E-325 Gas Grill (Liquid Propane)

title: Excellent grill

title: Wheels

title: Mixed review
text:
This is one of the best grills I have owned.  I gave only three stars because of some flaws.  The one-touch cleaning system is too flimsy; mine has shed two of the three "petals", significantly limiting my control of the airflow.  The other flaw is worse.  The cooking grate is chrome plated steel.  That is a stupid choice of material.  The chrome flakes off into the food over time, leading to corrosion of the underlying steel.  Worse, I'm feeding chrome flakes to my family.  I accessed Weber's parts list online, looking for a stainless steel grate.  Weber doesn't even make one.  I'll have to resort to an aftermarket grate.

Weber's classic bowl design is so well designed and well manufactured, it's a mystery to me why they would put such a cheap piece of garbage as their grate in their signature grill.  A mystery and a disappointment.

title: Sear Zone!

title: Weber never disappoints

text: I don't like that you can't see the burners light like you could on the previous model. The cheap starter, only two wheels instead of four and plastic side shelves support my claim.

title: 2019 Spirit still performing admirably
text: 2019 Grill going strong   Replaced two components due to wear. Covered by warranty. Excellent customer service.

title: Hot stuff
text: We love our little Weber Spirit grill. It is usable year round, unlike other lightly constructed grills. Weber has been terrific about replacing damaged warranted parts due to unexpected accidents, as well! It’s been a great value.

title: Doesn't work well
text: I'm very disappointed as I've had Weber grills in the past. They've been awesome! But this one seems to have issues with heating up. It often runs only up to 200°. It's very hard to grill with the temperature so low. I worked with customer service and it's still having that issue.

title: Spirit II E-310 is the perfect grill for me
text: I've been grilling on Webers since 1985 when I got my first 18" coal bbq.  I had that one (seriously) for more than 30 years, and replaced it with a 22" coal grill with the rotisserie insert.  We moved to Hawaii and I had to get a gas grill for the lanai.  I chose the Spirit II E-310 over a larger unit because it does everything I need it to do and can still be moved easily to make use of our limited space.  I just got a rotisserie attachment, and inaugurated it with a whole chicken that turned out fabulously.  It heats up quickly, cooks everything evenly and well, and cleans up easily.  Couldn't be happier with this gas grill.

title: Great grill, but…
text: Cooks great!!! Perfect size. Many improvements over my 25 year oid Genesis.  BUT, needs casters on left side!  How could you miss this. Maybe offer a kit for caster upgrade.

title: Love the grill!!!
text: Love the grill! I had forgotten how good food cooked with charcoal tasted. This grill is very versatile. The only thing I can’t quite get the hang of is hanging the lid on the edge of the grill. I have to kind look for the hook as it attaches to the grill’s edge. It hangs well but takes a moment to get it right. I love the ash catcher and the rotating holes in which the ashes fall into the catcher. So easy and mess free!

title: Great Grill!
text: Perfect size for 2 people. Not too heavy to move where we want it for cooking or storage

title: A Great Little Grill!
text: I was a bit skeptical that this little grill could make delicious burgers, roasts, and chicken. The first thing I made were burgers that turned out so juicy, a little smoky, and beautifully grilled. I reverse seared a roast, a spatchcock chicken covering the grates with foil for indirect heat that all came out perfect. I think the enamel coated cast iron grate design makes all the difference, and it prevents flare ups.

title: Weber E-325 should have had included
text: Dear Weber, I have been using Weber products for over 25 years and have always been completely satisfied until I purchased my new Spirit E-325 grill. The grill works perfectly but is missing two key items that my original Spirit had. One is a set of wheels on the front to move it easily and the second is a built-in tank scale that shows the remaining fuel.  I would gladly paid more for the grill if these two items were included.

title: Avoid this grill if it is subject to wind
text: Don't buy this grill.  The back is completely open to the wind which reduces the temperature by several hundred degrees.  Neither Weber or third party suppliers have a fix.

title: Great Grill
text: Haven't been able to have a charcole grill for years now, have really missed it. Love the ash basket. Makes cleanup alot easier. The temp gage is also a nice plus !!

title: Great little grill
text: Easy assembly, excellent small grill for use on our deck. Easy to use and along with even heat for easy grilling.

title: Juik
text: Peace of crap. I have always had a Weber. That’s going to change. The grill shaped the second time we used it.

title: Ship item damaged
text: Lowes delivery team, knowingly delivered the grill damaged and rather than selecting a grill that wasn't damage, delivered it anyways. Weber learned of this after writing the first review and reached out and offered to send a replacement for the damage piece. Great customer service on Weber's part!! Shame on Lowes!!

title: Great basic grill!
text: Easy to light and clean. Most importantly easy to use with predictable great results!

title: Not up to former Spirit standards
text: Replaced previous 10 yr old Weber spirit but immediately noticed it much more difficult to move due to only 2 wheels vs old grill that had 4 wheels , uncertain  it ignites, plus missing rear panel so drip pan fills with rain water. …. Not Happy !

title: So good
text: Heaven in a kettle. I love it so far, two decades of gas grilling was a waste. Hank Hill can eat his heart out because I like tasting the heat and the meat.

title: Love my weber
text: Always wanted a weber BBQ. So happy I finally bought one. I wasn't looking for a huge bbq so purchasing the Sprit E 325 has been perfect. I love how the ignition process is so easy and achieving high temperature is very fast. I'm extremely satisfied with this purchase.

title: Manageable size and weight
text: Good product. I was surprised it needed assembly. The grill could be thrown out. It's under the base of the box.

title: Best little grill in Florida
text: Best 2-4 people grill ever, whether you’re cooking for a whole family or just several people. This is the Grille that does it all. The Weber name made me buy another one so now I have two.

title: Wheels are Horrible! CS reps have their hands tied
text: So hard to move around!! Loved my past Weber grills. Between not having a handle on the sides, and being stored on un-even ground, this grill needs to be moved when in use. With no casters, and none available for this model, we plan on getting rid of this grill and purchasing an alternate brand due to your inability to even SUGGEST a way to make it easier to move, or some sort of alterative. What a mistake to go Weber if your own customer service reps aren't given a way to help consumers. I need a serial number before you can help me?? Really?

title: Must have
text: Classic for a reason.  It does not have bells and whistles because you don’t need them.

title: Weber 22”
text: Great grill and great customer service! Love the quality of the grill. I had the grate lose a few welds and Weber sent me a new great fast!

title: Best Grill Ever
text: Best grill out there for regular cooking.  Well constructed and sears meat just like a restaurant!

title: Spirit E-325 grill, one month into ownership...
text: Grill is well built, with a removable main lower pan making cleaning a breeze. Heat is even, and easily controlled with three control knobs. Lighting is easy through use of control knobs. Temperature gage is useful and very readable. Grates clean easily. Recommend using Mr Bar-B-Que scrubber (Walmart) as it leaves no steel bristles behind, and is easy on porcelain coated grates.

title: great new weber
text: new spirit e-325 BBQ replaces our old genesis 1000 .New unit assembly was quick and easy,great instructions.First use was great. Hope it lasts as long as the old one.

title: Arrived with damaged lid and one touch ash holder
text: I ordered the Weber Master Touch Kettle Grill in Deep Ocean Blue online from the Home Depot on May 8 for my husband for Father’s Day. When I got it the box was double taped, I didn’t think anything of it. The ash catcher holder was so bent it wouldn’t stay on, and the lid was bent and scratched up. I contacted Weber online and sent the pictures and proof of purchase, they sent me a new one touch circle ash catcher, and then the new lid. The new lid came in worse shape than the original one, the box was pretty smashed and when I opened it the lid was shaped like an oval! We haven’t even got to use it yet. They say they are out of the lids and will send one when they are back in stock. I’m ready to take the grill back to Home Depot for a refund!

text: BEEN WAITING FOR THE ELECTRIC IGNITER, RECEIVED THE THERMOSTAT BUT STILL CANT USE.  ;O(  SO MUCH FOR SUMMER BBQ

title: Small but mighty
text: Now that summer is now here I’ve been enjoying grilling some meat and having some amazing family time. This charcoal grill is so easy to assemble and clean. It’s incredibly useful and great for a quick meal.

title: Weber 3 burner
text: This is our first Weber grill.  It is very well built and built to last.  It is the perfect size.  Highly recommend for everyone needing to replace their grill.

title: First Weber Gas Grill Purchase
text: I replaced my old gas grill with this grill. This is my first time to buy a Weber grill. I've cooked twice and really like the performance. I really like the sear feature particularly when cooking steaks. During assembly it seems to be well constructed and should last years to come. The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is the lack of castor wheels. It's makes moving the grill a challenge particularly for senior folks. The design team for this grill is dummer than a box of rocks. Why in the heck would you not have wheels at all for corners? Okay Weber... I've read in other reviews this is an issue. Of course the reply is you'll forward this issue on to someone else. Well... now do something about it like offer a retro kit to add two castor wheels in place of the two support feet. Also... on the next generation model tell the design team to put wheels on all for corners. It's just common sense which there's not much of that anymore.

title: Purchase & product review from a gas grill rookie
text: I had never cooked on a gas grill until I purchased the Weber Spirit E-325, so I am still in the learning process. The purchase at ACE Hardware was smooth and I was very happy with the free assembly and delivery in very good condition. So far, everything has worked quite smoothly. I do need to learn more about temperature control, but am otherwise quite satisfied with this product. I'm giving this 4 stars out of five simply because I'm still in the learning mode.

title: Grill all summer

title: A Beautiful Choice
text: This modest sized barbeque is terrific. Heats up quickly, and has a special sear level to help create a lovely crust on a piece of beef. Large enough grill area for grilling things like chicken thighs, or chicken breasts, with comfortable space to move things around for different levels of heat.

Loved the old one. this one is better. would recommend to anyone

title: Meets all your camping needs.
text: A great little camping grill.  Compact and versatile.

title: Hard To Start
text:
I purchased the Spirit E-325 grill to replace an older Spirit 325.  The new model is not as well built, lacks a back panel, has only two wheels so it can't be pulled forward, replaces chrome side tables with plastic and does not have a tank hanger/gauge.  And, the burner area is smaller than the old model although both have three burners.
My biggest issue is that it is harder to start.  If you open the tank valve too fast, the regulator jams up.  After slowly opening the tank, if you do not then hold the burner knob for a few seconds after the click, it does not light.  The old system was simply to open the tank and push the electric lighter.  Not an improvement.
The sear zone burners do get very hot though.

Definitely not an upgrade to the old model.

title: Almost perfect
text: Being a three burner grill, it should have four wheels instead of two. It’s a pain trying to maneuver it where needed.  Also, a metal plate across the back would be nice to keep the flame from going out when it’s windy outside.

title: Reasons to purchase a Weber
text: Bought my first Weber in 1980, used it for 11 years, bought a house with an installed gas grill. Eventually went back to charcoal grill, however, not a Weber. After many years and various charcoal grills, bought a new Weber. Wow, built in thermometer, new style grate making it easy to add more charcoal if necessary when smoking food and a new way to dispose of the ashes. Excellent modifications!

title: Weber E325
text: Love my Weber E325 gas grill! It is the perfect size for my location. Cooks evenly and the sear zone is amazing! Best looking and best tasting ribeyes I ever cooked!. The quality of the grill is what you expect from Weber!

title: New grill has issues, not working properly.

Our old Weber was 22 years old, and still worked great. Decided to up grade. First burner and second light first time. The third burner has to try 4-5 times before it will light.
Disappointed that he brand new grill has issues. Tested gas pressure with a monometer and it is set at 10.5 inches of water column.

title: Weber The one and only Grill
text: I always recommend a Weber to all my friends and family, the best grill ever made, my first grill lasted 20 years with no issues, I just replaced it

title: Unbelievable
text: We went to Lowe’s to replace our 15+ Genesis grill by Weber. We did not need a big grill so we decided to get the E-325 Gas grill. I registered the grill but I got a continual denial indicating that I was putting the wrong serial number. I’m talking resubmitting 5x at least. Finally, I contacted customer service via email. Their response was that they registered the grill for me. That’s all they said - they registered it for me. The first time to start/light, it fired right up. But, it did not stay lit. Frustrating. All 3 burners lit but none stayed lit. Customer service was called. I was asked to give the serial number of the grill. I explained what had happened in my initial attempt to register this but I felt I was not being heard. A language barrier ? Anyhow, I was asked to provide a picture of the serial number and send the pic via email. After (10) min of email it was established that this serial number did not exist. After 25-30 minute exchange of information to establish my identity, my address, my email and faulty serial number we finally got to the issue. I was told I had a faulty magneto and that a part would be sent. In the meantime, manual lighting would have to be used but that still did not keep the burners lit. This phone call was 15 June. I called back 24 June to get an order update. I was informed that there was no part on the way. Did I misunderstand via another language barrier that I was told no part was on the way ?  She knew what part I needed was the most frustrating part. I told her that I would be taking this grill back to Lowe’s for a refund, which I did. The one thing besides a working grill that I’m disappointed in is that there isn’t a gauge where to hang the propane tank and the volume can be monitored for capacity and not have to guess.

title: Great for barbecue great hest control.

.

If you use a griddle on the grates it won't go much over 300 degrees but will def cook an egg at that temp. - If I was going to buy a grill for a gift, I don't think I would pay the price for this one but now that we have it, I will learn to enjoy it.

title: Weber is the best.
text: Grea grill.  Very reliable and easy to start and keep clean.

title: So far, so good.
text: I've only used the grill once, and it's going to take a bit of getting used to. I had a smoker with a side firebox before, so this is considerably different. I am really happy with the grill so far. Assembly was simple.

title: A small dynamo that works great!
text: Owned a Weber for many years. This is my first Spirit. Like the newer ignition system, the sear feature and foldable shelves for storage. Preheat times are short and I have not found any hot spots that will cause burning. Overall, we love it.

title: Poor Quality for the money
text: I'm an idiot for buying this grill without looking at it in person. Paid $500 on sale and it has the quality of a $199 grill.

title: Ignition Problem

I couldn’t get the burners to ignite. I returned it and bought another brand. I have owned Weber grills for years. This is very disappointing.

title: Nice unit
text:

Features are great from the searing area to regular usage. 
Works perfect for two to four people but can handle six.
Temperatures vary but easy enough to adjust for different dishes once you have used it couple of times. We got the grill accessories to go with it and are glad we did. Glad we purchased it instead of a larger one.

title: Great grill
text: Love it. Large cooking area. The only think it lacks is something onhtge damper for adjusting. Too hot to touch while cooking.

title: ES 325 little view
text:
Drill are with sear zone excellent for high low temp grilling. My first 2" steak turned out awesome with reverse searing. 
LUV IT!

title: A fine gas grill that I expect to use for years!
text: An excellent smaller grill that is perfect for a couple or small BBQ gatherings. Assembly was straightforward and the instructions reasonably clear. A second person is helpful at a couple steps. Grill is very sturdy and seems durable. Grates are heavy duty. The sear zone works great for steaks and chops. I’ve owned 4-5 Weber grills and generally get 10+ years out of them because of the design, quality materials, and parts availability. The one time I tried a competitive brand I had to replace grates and other parts too frequently, it was harder to clean, and was entering end of life in about 6 years.

title: Love Weber Grill
text: It would have only given it 4 stars because it came damaged.  Weber promptly corrected the issue so that was excellent!

title: Great little grill
text: We looked at gas grills for several weeks before pulling the trigger on this one. It’s perfect for 2-4 folks. It has a small footprint and is so easy to use. We love it and would recommend this purchase,

title: Awesome kettle grill.
text: The apex of kettles. Easy to use , tons of available extras to buy to personalize to your needs.  Super versatile

title: Super Annoying

title: Perfect for us

This thing is built well, from quality materials, and regulates the heat very well, no hot or cold spots that I’ve found. It’s just my wife and I now, so we didn’t need a huge grill, and I still have my smoker for the big jobs… this grill is Perfect for us, and our needs!

title: Great Grill
text: Great charcoal grill! We’ve only used once so far. But the pork chops tasted delicious.

title: For entry level, it is a good grill

title: Perfect

title: Good so far.

text: Excellent grille for the price. The Sear section can get up to 650 degree!  The individual fire starters are a big improvement over the push buttons. The only downer is the oil drip pan.  It must be tilted to remove and then any liquids are spilled inside the cabinet.

title: Great Grill

title: Amazing!

title: Nice grill

title: Excellent in every way

I did replace grates and heat reflectors, but overall it served me well. But this grill, though smaller, seems like a big upgrade. title: Excellent design and function

The sear settings work perfectly for cooking game meats while I can cook vegetables at the same time at lower temps on the other burner. Grill size is adequate and more efficient than the Genesis for my uses. The modern design is well thought out with nice features such as silicon bumpers on the lid for quiet, gentle closing, and wheels large enough to move easily. Dropping the side tables makes for a minimal foot print which I had not been concerned about but appreciate now.

title: Assembling The Grill
text:
The old grill I was replacing had the larger wheels on the right just like the Weber and smaller ones on spindles on the left that made moving it easy.  The place on my patio where I keep the grill is in a place where if assembled as shown, I would have to lift the grill from the right table and DRAG the grill on the fixed feet until it was clear to the point I could move it away from the house.  Not exactly optimal!

I contacted Weber and asked them if I could assemble it with the wheels on the left.  They steadfastly told me it was not recommended to make any changes.  However, when I was putting it together it became clear that all four corners at the bottom where the wheels and feet go were identical, so I put it together with the wheels on the left.  I told Weber that they should make that an option so folks could assemble it to suit their needs.

Weber got all testy with me saying it was dangerous (but didn't say how, because that's impossible) and said it could void my warranty.  PULEEEZE!

For what it's worth, I'm a retired professional firefighter, 30 years.  I understand risk/reward assessments.  There is no way on Earth that doing what I did created a hazard.  In fact, it could be argued that dragging it on the feet to get it away from the house, eventually ruining the feet could create a hazard!

For the life of me, I can't understand why, oh why, Weber is so obtuse!

title: Master touch 22
text:
I purchased the Weber Master-Touch 22 after my previous grill names after the little French emperor had reached the end of its life. I decided to give Weber a try because I had heard good things about the brand, and as an experienced BBQ enthusiast, I was genuinely looking forward to using it. I especially enjoy South American-style BBQ, so I have fairly high expectations when it comes to charcoal grilling.

Unfortunately, my experience with this grill has been extremely disappointing.

My biggest issue is the shallow cooking depth and the fact that the cooking grate cannot be adjusted in height. With the way I like to cook, this makes it very difficult to control the heat and distance from the charcoal. Almost everything I cook ends up getting deeply burned, even when I carefully manage the charcoal.

Controlling the amount and placement of charcoal to achieve the right cooking temperature is also much harder than I expected. For someone who has been BBQing for years, I find the lack of control particularly frustrating.

I really wanted to like this grill, but I am having a terrible time with it. I am deeply disappointed with the Weber Master-Touch 22 and honestly wish I had never purchased it.

title: Cheap plastic gas line connection
text: I bought a Weber because I believed it was a good company with quality products. I used the grill 3 times. On the fourth use, as soon as I started to turn the propane on I could hear a hiss and smell gas. Finding the Weber website to report the issue wasn't the problem. The problem was trying to contact Weber customer service--definitely not a user friendly process. After a lot of frustration, I finally found a form to fill out and submitted it. I immediately got a response, which requested that I submit a clear photo of the black ring in the propane tank. Once again, I got an immediate response that said I would be shipped a replacement part and would received it within 3-5 business days upon notification of shipping. That was three weeks ago and I have never been given any shipping notification information.  Every time I try to check status on the Weber website, I get a message that says: "For technical reasons, your request could not be handled properly at this time. We apologize for any inconvenience." If it was easier to report a problem and get a replacement part, I would have given 4 stars instead of 1. Also, the plastic connections cheapened an otherwise nice product.

title: Unhappy with this one
text:
I’m actually sorry that I bought this unit. It had so many good reviews, and I don’t need a large grill, but my old rounded top Grill worked better.
I find the greats are too far apart. It uses much more gas than my old unit. And it just doesn’t cook as well. The one page of instructions in the booklet are for one hard to read because they’re in tiny print, but they don’t really get into the subtlety or not so subtle aspects of grilling things on this grill. Even when I use the enhanced boost function on two of the grills, I don’t get a nice Seer the way I did on my old model. I think Weber, it would be great if you actually created a handout and/or some YouTube videos showing people actually cooking different food on this grill from beginning to end. There’s plenty of stuff about how to light it and basically heat it up.
In terms of its size and maneuverability it’s just fine. The new coating on the fold up ledges is great except it’s very slippery. So if you put a plate or Pyrex on it, you have to put as I do some kind of gripper underneath or it’ll slide right off.
And I would love to understand why it uses up so much propane. The old Grill would last seemingly forever. I’ve only cooked maybe 6 to 8 small items on this grill and it used 3/4 of the tank.
Anyway, I am not a fan of this model. And I’m sorry I bought it.
